Quick Answer
macOS 27 Golden Gate has far more useful features than the ones you will notice immediately after updating. I tested more than 27 of them and picked the 27 worth trying, including Siri AI, custom Safari extensions, smarter Shortcuts, new Photos tools, and several smaller additions. Go through this list, and you will likely find a few features that can make the way you use your Mac easier.
Apple has finally released macOS 27 Golden Gate, and unlike the last few macOS updates, this one feels like a much bigger update. Apple has changed how macOS looks, added the new Siri AI, brought several Apple Intelligence features to its built-in apps, and made noticeable changes to Safari, Photos, Notes, Calendar, and many other places that you will notice once you start using your Mac.
I have been using macOS 27 and trying these features on my Mac, and some of them are genuinely useful. Some of my favorites is the new Siri that does many more things than previous, also Safari that lets you create your own extension simply by describing what you want it to do.
There are plenty of smaller additions like this throughout macOS 27. Some solve problems I have had with macOS for a long time, while others add things that previously required a third-party app or a much longer workaround. In this article, I will show you the best macOS 27 Golden Gate features I have found so far, what has changed, and how you can try them on your Mac.
Table of Contents
27 Best macOS 27 Golden Gate Features
macOS 27 Golden Gate comes with countless new features and small changes, and covering every single one of them in one article isn’t possible. After digging deeper into the update and trying many of these features myself, I have picked the best 27 that I found the most useful and that I think most Mac users should know about. Some are easy to notice, while others are hidden inside the apps and settings you already use every day.
Talk With Siri AI and Continue Your Previous Conversations
Siri has received one of its biggest changes on the Mac with macOS 27. Instead of only appearing as the small Siri interface we have been using for years, Siri AI now has its own app where you can start a conversation, ask follow-up questions, and return to your previous conversations later.
This is particularly useful when I have already given Siri all the context about something, and whenever needed, I can reopen that conversation instead of explaining everything again.
To use the Siri AI app on your Mac, first make sure Siri is enabled.
Once it is enabled, open the Siri app, where you will find all your previous conversations in the left sidebar and the chat window on the right. You can select any previous conversation to continue chatting or start a new conversation with Siri. If you right-click on any conversation in the sidebar, you will also see additional options to pin or delete the conversation.
Search Your Mac and Ask Siri Directly From Spotlight
Spotlight is one of the features I use almost every day on my Mac. With macOS 27, it also becomes a quick way to access Siri AI, so I don’t have to open the dedicated Siri app whenever I have a small question.
You just have to press Command + Space to open Spotlight and continue typing normally when you want to find an app, file, document, or setting. When you want to ask Siri AI something instead, just type your query normally and hit return to get an answer. You can also access whatever you have searched in Spotlight in the dedicated Siri app as a separate conversation.
I prefer using this for quick questions and keeping the Siri app for longer conversations where I know I will need follow-up questions.
Create Your Own Safari Extension Just by Describing It
Safari already supports extensions, but I still have to find an extension that does exactly what I need. With macOS 27, I can simply describe the functionality I want, and Safari can create an extension for me using Apple Intelligence.
I tried this with Instagram. I sometimes watch Reels on Instagram’s website, but it doesn’t give me a playback bar to quickly move forward or backward in a Reel. Instead of searching for an extension, I asked Safari to create one using this prompt:
Prompt: Create an extension for Instagram that adds playback controls to Reels and lets me move forward or backwards in the video while watching a Reel.
Surprisingly, it worked. After enabling the generated extension, I could seek forward and backwards while watching Instagram Reels. If there is a small website-specific feature you have always wanted, this gives you a way to try building it yourself.
To create one:
- Open Safari on your Mac and visit the website for which you want to create an extension.
- Click on the Page menu inside Safari’s address bar and select Describe Extension.
- Describe exactly what you want the extension to do. “I recommend keeping the request focused on one particular problem instead of asking it to change several unrelated things on the website.”
- Safari will first check whether an existing extension from the App Store can do what you described. If you don’t want one of the suggested extensions, click Create to generate your own.
- Once Safari creates the extension, click Try and test it on the website. Don’t save it immediately; use the website normally for a few minutes and make sure the extension actually behaves the way you expected.
- If something isn’t working correctly, click Edit and describe what you want Safari to change. Once you are happy with the result, click Save to keep the extension.
If you are new to browser extensions, you can check our list of the best Safari extensions for Mac to see what else extensions can add to Safari.
Create Shortcuts by Simply Explaining What You Want
Shortcuts can automate plenty of repetitive tasks on a Mac, but creating a complicated shortcut manually isn’t always easy. macOS 27 lets you describe what you want in normal language, and Apple Intelligence can put together the required Shortcut actions for you.
For example, I created a simple shortcut for work. Whenever I start working, I need to open TechPP, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress. Instead of opening each website manually, I created a shortcut that opens all four websites in Chrome whenever I run it.
Prompt: Create a shortcut that opens techpp.com, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress in Chrome.
Here’s how you can create it:
- Open the Shortcuts app on your Mac and click the plus (+) button.
- Enter the prompt in the Describe a shortcut field and let Apple Intelligence create the shortcut for you.
- Once it is created, click Run or the Play icon to test it.
Use Visual Intelligence to Understand What’s on Your Screen
Visual Intelligence on the Mac works differently from the camera-based experience on the iPhone. In macOS 27, I can select something already visible on my screen and ask Siri AI about it, which is useful when the thing I am looking at is easier to show than describe.
Suppose I see a chair in an image and want to know what kind of chair it is or find similar designs. Instead of describing its shape, material, and appearance, I can press Command + Shift + 6, select the chair on the screen, and choose Ask Siri to ask about it. There is also an Image Search option when I want to find visually similar results online.
Adjust How Much Liquid Glass You Want on Your Mac
Apple introduced Liquid Glass across its operating systems last year, but macOS 27 now gives you more control over how transparent the interface actually looks. Instead of having to accept one fixed appearance, there is now a slider that lets you choose how clear or tinted you want Liquid Glass to be.
To adjust it:
- Open the System Settings on your Mac and click Appearance in the sidebar.
- Find the Liquid Glass adjustment inside the Appearance settings.
- Move the slider toward the left if you want the interface to look clearer and more transparent. Move it toward the right if you want more tint and less of the background showing through.
Hide Extra Menu Bar Icons and Access Them When You Need Them
My Mac’s menu bar gets crowded quickly because several utilities I use throughout the day add their own icons. macOS 27 handles this better with a new overflow control that hides icons when there isn’t enough space and gives you a double-arrow button to reveal them whenever you need them. This means I don’t have to remove a useful menu bar utility just because I don’t need its icon visible every minute. This is especially useful on MacBooks with a notch, where menu bar space is already limited.
Let Safari Automatically Organise Your Tabs Into Topics
I am terrible at keeping my browser tabs under control, particularly when I am researching something and have several unrelated pages open at the same time. Safari already has Tab Groups on Mac, which are useful when you manually organize related tabs. macOS 27 takes this a step further by using Apple Intelligence to automatically identify related tabs and organize them into topics. Each topic gets a label and a tab count, and you can collapse a topic when you aren’t working on it without actually closing those tabs.
For example, while researching for this article, I might have 10–15 tabs open about different macOS features, along with a few Amazon shopping tabs and some work-related pages. Instead of showing all of them together in one long row, Safari can automatically identify which tabs are related and organise them into separate topics such as macOS 27, Shopping, and Work. I can keep the macOS 27 topic expanded while I am researching and collapse Shopping and Work to hide those tabs temporarily. Whenever I need them again, I can simply expand that topic without having to search through all my open tabs.
To enable it:
- Open Safari on your Mac and click Safari in the menu bar at the top left of the screen.
- Choose Settings, and then switch to Tabs section.
- Then click the drop-down menu right to Organise tabs and select Automatically Create Topics.
- Continue browsing normally and open a few pages related to the same subject. Safari will identify related tabs and place them under a topic when it recognises the connection.
Change the Perspective of a Photo With Reframe
Cropping can remove unnecessary space from a photo, but it can’t change the angle from which the photo appears to have been taken. The new Reframe feature goes further by using Apple Intelligence to change the perspective and angle of an existing image.
I find this useful when I like a photo but wish I had taken it from a slightly different angle or positioned the subject differently. To use it:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo.
- Click the Edit button in the top-right corner to open the photo editing tools.
- Click Tools and select Reframe from the available options.
- Drag the photo or use the available perspective controls to change how you want the final image to be framed. I recommend making smaller adjustments first instead of immediately trying to create a completely different camera angle.
- Once you have the angle you want, click Reframe and wait for Apple Intelligence to generate the additional parts required for the new perspective.
- Pay particular attention to faces, hands, and other objects whose shape is easy to recognize. If everything looks right, Finally click Save Changes.
Expand a Photo Beyond Its Original Frame With Extend
There have been times when I had a good portrait photo but couldn’t use it as a wallpaper or inside a presentation because converting it to a wider aspect ratio would crop an important part of the image, and where the new Extend feature comes in. It generate additional content outside the original frame with Apple Intelligence.
To try it, open the image in Photos, click Edit, and open Tools. Select Extend, drag the edges beyond the original photo or choose the aspect ratio you need, and click Extend to generate the missing area.
Check the newly generated areas carefully before saving the result. If you don’t like what it created, adjust the frame and try again instead of keeping an obviously generated section.
Remove Unwanted Objects From Photos With Clean Up
Apple introduced the Clean Up tool with Apple Intelligence, and macOS 27 improves how it handles larger unwanted objects. If I take a photo at a tourist spot and someone is standing in the background I can select that person and let Photos remove them.
Here’s how you can remove an unwanted object from a photo:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo you want to edit.
- Click Edit in the upper-right corner and open Tools.
- Select Clean Up, and your Mac will analyse the image. In some cases, Photos may automatically highlight objects it thinks you might want to remove.
- Click on a highlighted object to remove it, or use the Erase brush to paint over the object yourself. You can also circle the object if that makes it easier to select.
- And, finally, click Clean Up.
Resize the iPhone Mirroring Window
iPhone Mirroring is useful when I want to access something on my iPhone without picking it up, but using everything inside a phone-sized window on a large Mac display isn’t always ideal. macOS 27 fixes this by letting you resize the iPhone Mirroring window just by dragging its corner. You can also use keyboard shortcuts to quickly resize the iPhone Mirroring window. Press Command + Plus (+) to increase the window size and Command + Minus (-) to decrease it. If you want to return the window to its default size, press Command + 0.
But macOS 27 takes resizing a step further with supported apps. When you open a resizable app and make the iPhone Mirroring window wider, the app can actually adjust its layout and show more content instead of simply making the same iPhone interface bigger.
For example, if I open a supported app and drag the iPhone Mirroring window into a wider layout, I can get more usable screen space and information inside the app. Not every app supports this yet, so in unsupported apps, resizing may simply make the existing interface larger or smaller. You can press Command + 9 whenever you want to return the window to the standard iPhone size.
Let Your Mac Suggest Better Names for Files and Folders
My Downloads folder has taught me how quickly bad filenames can become a problem. A name such as “Untitled” or “Document 2” becomes useless once I forget what is inside them.
With macOS 27, Apple Intelligence can suggest names for files and folders based on what they contain. Instead of having to open a document again just to remember what it was about, macOS can look at the content and suggest a name that actually describes it.
First, you have to make sure this feature is enabled on your Mac. To do so, open Finder and click the Finder button in the menu bar. Next, choose Settings and make sure you are in the General tab. Now, check the box next to Suggest Filenames.
Now, to use this feature, right-click any document, photo, screenshot, or folder in Finder and select Rename. Wait for around five seconds, and Finder will show you a few suggested names based on the file’s contents. You can select the name you like and use it instead of typing one manually.
Create and Edit Calendar Events by Describing Them
macOS 27 makes creating Calendar events faster by describing the event naturally instead of filling in every field separately. I can type something like “Pankaj’s birthday next Monday,” and Calendar can use those details to create the event.
To try it, open Calendar, click the plus (+) button, and enter your description in Describe Event. You can also describe changes to an existing event instead of manually changing individual details.
Draw Directly Inside Apple Notes on Your Mac
Not everything you want to save in a note needs to be written as text. For example, if you’re planning the layout of a room, sketching a quick idea, making a simple diagram, or noting down something that is easier to remember visually, a quick drawing can be more useful than typing it out. With macOS 27, you can now create these drawings directly inside a note on your Mac and keep them saved along with the rest of your notes.
Previously, you could create drawings in a note from an iPhone or iPad, but macOS didn’t let you draw directly inside Notes on the Mac. Now, you can use your mouse or trackpad to create a quick sketch without leaving the Notes app.
Here’s how you can draw inside a note:
- Open the Notes app.
- Click the Markup button in the Notes toolbar to open the drawing tools.
- Choose the drawing tool you want to use, and adjust its thickness and colour depending on what you are trying to draw.
- Start drawing directly inside the note using your mouse or trackpad.
- Once you are finished, click the Markup button again to exit the drawing tools and continue working on the rest of your note.
Generate Images in More Styles With Image Playground
I tested Image Playground on Mac when Apple first introduced it, and one of my biggest complaints was how limited the available styles felt. Now, Apple has made Image Playground much more flexible in macOS 27. You now get more styles, including create photorealistic images, and the Any Style option lets you describe the kind of visual appearance you want instead of choosing only from a small set of presets. You can also choose square, portrait, or landscape output depending on where you plan to use the image.
Another change I find more useful is targeted editing. If most of the generated image looks good but there is one part I want to change, I can select that area and describe the change instead of generating the entire image again and hoping everything else remains the same.
If you are using Image Playground for the first time, I recommend reading our complete Image Playground guide for Mac, where we have covered the interface, creating images, using your own photos, and managing generated images in more detail.
Record Your Mac Screen With System Audio
This is one of my favorite smaller additions in macOS 27, especially because I regularly work on tutorials. macOS has had a built-in screen recorder for a long time, but recording the sound coming directly from the Mac hasn’t been nearly as straightforward as recording the screen itself.
The difference between system audio and microphone audio is important here. If I am recording a tutorial and an app plays a sound, system audio captures that sound directly. I don’t have to turn up my MacBook speakers and let the microphone record them along with keyboard sounds, fan noise, and everything else happening in the room.
Here’s how you can record your Mac screen with system audio:
- Press Shift + Command + 5 on your keyboard to open the built-in screenshot and screen-recording toolbar.
- Choose whether you want to Record Entire Screen, Record Selected Portion, or Selected Window depending on what you want to capture.
- Click Options in the toolbar and enable Include System Audio so that sounds playing on your Mac are included in the recording.
Add Extra-Large Widgets to Your Mac Desktop
I have been using widgets on my Mac desktop since Apple introduced them with macOS Sonoma. but the existing widget sizes don’t always work when an app has more information to show.
macOS 27 adds new Extra Large widget sizes, including a portrait layout for supported widgets. The additional space lets apps show considerably more information on the desktop.
To add an extra large widget on your desktop:
- Right-click anywhere on your Mac desktop and select Edit Widgets.
- Find the app whose widget you want to add and look through the available widget sizes. If the app supports the new sizes, you should see Extra Large or Extra Large Portrait among the options.
- Select the size you want and add the widget to your desktop.
If you haven’t used desktop widgets before, we have a complete guide explaining how to add widgets to your Mac desktop, including how to customise the widgets already on your Mac.
Share Photos and Videos in Full Resolution With Shared Albums
Shared Albums are convenient when I want to collect photos from a trip, event, or family function in one place, but there has always been a compromise: the photos and videos shared through them weren’t necessarily kept in their original quality.
Apple changes that with the new Shared Albums experience in macOS 27. Newly created permanent Shared Albums can store photos and videos at full resolution
Let Android and Windows Users Add Photos to Your Shared Albums
The Shared Albums update gets even more useful if your friends or family don’t all use Apple devices. Previously, you needed several WhatsApp chats, Google Drive folders, and people sending pictures individually
With macOS 27, people on Android and Windows can access the updated Shared Albums through a web browser, and they don’t necessarily need an Apple Account to participate. More importantly, you can allow them to contribute photos instead of limiting them to viewing the album.
Save Any Frame From a Video Directly as a Photo
Sometimes the best photo from a moment is actually hidden inside a video. Before macOS 27, if we spotted an interesting moment in a video, the easiest way to save it as a photo was to take a screenshot. But a screenshot doesn’t preserve the video frame as cleanly as a dedicated photo, and you may end up with lower quality or unwanted elements from the screen. With macOS 27, you can now save any video frame directly as a separate photo in your Photos library.
Open the video in Photos, pause it at the moment you want, and check the nearby frames until you find the best one. Then right-click the frame and select Save Video Frame as Photo. The saved frame appears in your Photos library, where you can edit and share it just like any other photo.
Start a Slideshow Directly From a Photo Album
I usually organise photos from a trip or event into an album, but when I want to show those pictures to someone, opening them one by one isn’t the nicest way to do it. macOS 27 makes this easier by letting me start a slideshow directly from an album in Photos, so I can show the entire collection without having to open every photo individually.
Slideshows themselves aren’t new on the Mac, but I like that I can now start one directly from an album I have already organised. Once the slideshow starts, I can quickly customise how it plays by changing the transition and duration, adding music, and deciding whether it should loop.
Here’s how you can start a slideshow from an album:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and find the album you want to show.
- Control-click the album and select Start Slideshow from the menu.
- Once the slideshow starts, click Customise if you want to change how it plays.
- Adjust the Transition & Duration settings to control how quickly the photos move from one to another, and choose music if you want something playing in the background.
Change How Fast and Expressive Siri Sounds
I don’t always want Siri to speak at the same pace. If I am following instructions, a slightly slower response can be easier to understand. And if the current voice feels too slow, you can make it speak faster. macOS 27 also lets you change more than just how fast Siri speaks. On supported Macs and voices, you can also adjust how expressive the voice sounds. Increasing this setting gives Siri’s speech more variation and emphasis, which can make the spoken responses feel more natural and animated.
Get Better Resolution Support for External Displays
macOS 27 improves external display support, including 5K at 120Hz on certain compatible ultrawide monitors. Apple has also improved how macOS restores window positions and display arrangements after disconnecting and reconnecting a monitor, which I find more useful when regularly docking and undocking a MacBook.
After connecting your monitor, open System Settings, select Displays, and choose the external monitor to see the available resolutions and refresh rates.
Make Buttons and Other Controls Easier to See With Show Borders
macOS 27 adds a new Show Borders accessibility option that makes the boundaries around buttons and other interface controls easier to distinguish. This can be useful if you don’t want some controls to blend into the background with the Liquid Glass design.
To enable it, open System Settings and click Accessibility in the left sidebar. Select Display from the right-side panel, find Show Borders, and turn on the toggle next to it. You can also try Reduce Transparency from the same section if transparency itself is making parts of the interface difficult to see.
Explore Cities With More Detailed 3D Views in Apple Maps
Apple has improved the 3D city experience in Maps with more detailed buildings and surroundings in supported locations. I don’t use 3D Maps every time I need directions, but it can be useful when I want to understand the layout of an unfamiliar area before visiting it.
To try it, open Maps and search for the city or location you want to explore. Click View in the menu bar, select Show 3D Map, and enable Satellite if you want to explore the area using the detailed imagery.
Try the New Golden Gate Wallpapers and Screen Savers
Finally, macOS 27 comes with new Sunset and Night views of the Golden Gate Bridge, along with a new abstract wallpaper. The Golden Gate scenes can also be used as screen savers.
To try them, open System Settings and select Wallpaper from the left sidebar. Browse through the new macOS 27 backgrounds and select the one you want to use.
macOS 27 Feels More Useful Once You Start Finding the Smaller Changes
After trying more than 27 new macOS 27 features, creating custom Safari extensions is still the one I enjoyed the most, while several smaller additions have also made my everyday Mac experience better. If you enjoyed this guide, also check out our 27 best iOS 27 features you should try on your iPhone.
FAQs about macOS 27
1. Do All macOS 27 Features Work on Every Mac That Supports macOS 27?
No. Your Mac may support macOS 27 but still miss some features because individual features can have additional hardware, language, or region requirements.
2. Can Safari Extensions I Create Be Shared With Other People?
Not directly. Safari’s Describe Extension feature creates custom extensions for your own use. You can sync compatible extensions across your own Apple devices, but Apple currently doesn’t provide an option to send a generated extension directly to another person.
3. Can I Downgrade to macOS 26 After Installing macOS 27?
Yes, as long as macOS 26 supports your Mac. However, downgrading isn’t available like a normal software update and may require erasing your Mac and reinstalling the older macOS version. So, make sure you have a complete backup before proceeding.

How to check the temperature of your PC's CPU
There's some solid free software that can help you keep tabs on your computer's health.
The temperature of your CPU is one of those things you don't really think about unless something is wrong with your PC. When it's working, this tiny chip makes everything you do on your computer — from having multiple browser tabs open to editing photos and playing your favorite games — run smoothly.
But if your PC is suddenly more sluggish than usual or your fan is starting to sound like a jet engine, there's a good chance it could be overheating and the culprit might be your CPU.
Don't panic! The CPU's temperature can fluctuate for a lot of different reasons, and there are several free tools available that can tell you how it's doing.
Monitoring the temperature of your CPU
One of the best tools you can use to check the temperature of your CPU is HWiNFO, a free diagnostic tool that gives you a ton of real-time data about the hardware in your PC or laptop. Once installed, open the program and click on the Sensors tab to bring up a new window with temperature readings (displayed in Celsius) about your CPU.
There are other free apps like Core Temp and HWMonitor that can provide the same information as well. Whichever you choose, it can be helpful to turn them on every so often to see how your CPU is doing under different conditions. For example, you can fire up a game, video editing software or some other resource-intensive program to see how the CPU temperature changes compared to idle.
While the exact figures vary by CPU, an average running temperature of 60 degrees Celsius or below is typically considered a good baseline for everyday use. But if the CPU is consistently hovering between 70 to 90 degrees Celsius, you should look into what's causing the spike and if it's becoming a long-term problem. Pushing 90 degrees and above could indicate some serious overheating and might reduce the CPU's lifespan if it doesn't cool down.
You'll know ahead of time if it gets to that point: Most modern CPUs will throttle performance once the temperature is too high, significantly slowing down your PC as a way of protecting itself. But if throttling still isn't enough to cool the CPU, you might also experience freezing and crashes.
Keep in mind that these temperature readings are just guidelines and that your experience will vary depending on which CPU model you have. But if you're curious about pushing the limits of your processor (like overclocking for better performance), it's best to consult the original manufacturer for more accurate temperature ranges.
What do you do if it's running hot?
There are a few steps you can take if your CPU is running hotter than normal. It might be as simple as getting rid of a program that's eating up all your processing power — you can test this yourself by opening up Windows Task Manager and closing any apps that could be taxing the CPU.
But if the temperature still doesn't drop, your PC might have more of a hygiene problem than a software one. You can open up your tower to see if any dust has accumulated in the fans or on the components themselves. Use a can of compressed air to push the dust out and improve the airflow in your case. Many cases also have dust filters that can be removed and cleaned out.
You might also need to reapply thermal paste on the CPU, which can dry up over time. The paste serves as a thin layer of connection between the CPU and its heatsink, helping dissipate heat as the temperature rises. This isn't particularly challenging to do yourself, but will require temporarily removing the cooling hardware from your CPU, so find a good guide online and follow along.
The temperature of your CPU is just one indicator of your PC's overall health. But in a time where the price of PCs and laptops have sharply increased due to the AI bubble, it's more important than ever to be proactive about taking care of your electronics.
In addition to GPUs, RAM, and storage, prices of CPUs have been steadily climbing. Earlier this year, both AMD and Intel — two of the biggest chip manufacturers for PCs — increased their CPU prices and reportedly plan on doing it again. So normal check-ups like this can help extend the longevity of your PC and avoid the need to buy costly replacement parts.

One day after he rejected an Iranian proposal to end the war, President Trump told Axios in a phone interview on Sunday that he expects U.S. negotiators to engage in more talks with the country this week.
Why it matters: Qatar and other regional mediators are trying to revive negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, but the two sides are far apart on the key issues.
While Iran wants to focus any talks on the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. naval blockade, the Trump administration is demanding that Iran agree to nuclear concessions.
Two regional sources confirmed Trump's comment about more talks this week. They said they expect another round of indirect dialogue between the U.S. and Iran as early as Monday. But it isn't clear if the gaps can be bridged.
What he's saying: "I expect more talks with Iran [this week]. They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make. It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand," Trump said.
Asked if he is considering resuming strikes against Iran, Trump said: "I am always thinking about it."
State of play: In the meantime, Trump said, the U.S. military is facilitating a lot of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz.
He said that over the weekend the largest amount of oil transited through the strait since the war began. "More than 20 million barrels," Trump said.
A U.S. defense official confirmed Trump's assertion, saying that on Friday night 22 million barrels of oil were exported through the strait.
Driving the news: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held a new round of indirect negotiations with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York last Tuesday.
Qatari officials participated, passing messages between the two sides.
Araghchi delivered to Witkoff and Kushner Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear talks.
Iran proposed reopening the strait and restarting nuclear talks in a week, if the U.S. lifts its naval blockade, removes sanctions on oil sales and reinstates a ceasefire across the region.
Trump rejected the Iranian proposal on Saturday.
Behind the scenes: But a U.S. official and two regional sources told Axios that Qatari mediators are continuing shuttle diplomacy to try to reach a deal.
On Thursday, the prime minister of Qatar met in New York with the Iranian president and discussed the potential deal with the Trump administration.
Shortly after, senior Qatari officials met Witkoff and briefed him.
A regional source with knowledge of the indirect negotiations said the Qatari mediators discussed the original Iranian proposal with both parties and provided a compromise proposal to both sides to review.
What to watch: Over the weekend, the Qatari mediators have been going back and forth separately with Iranian and U.S. negotiators on changes to the text.
Qatari mediators are expected to meet separately with Araghchi and Witkoff as early as Monday.
The other side: Araghchi told NBC on Sunday that despite Trump's rejection of the Iranian proposal, Iran still wants a diplomatic solution.
He said that the midterm elections aren't part of Iran's calculations. "We only care about our national interests. We are ready for negotiations," he said.
"Although we heard from President Trump that he's rejecting this deal ... we are still waiting for an official response through the mediators," Araghchi added.

Super League Grand Final: Wakefield Trinity boss Daryl Powell on 'phenomenal, immense' run to title at Old Trafford
Wakefield Trinity comprehensively beat Warrington Wolves in Super League Grand Final on Saturday to clinch first league title for 58 years, becoming sixth team to win Super League; Wakefield were relegated in 2023, playing the 2024 season in the Championship under head coach Daryl Powell
Saturday 3 October 2026 23:03, UK
Wakefield Trinity head coach Daryl Powell revealed members of his playing squad were in shock following their stunning Super League Grand Final victory, two years on from playing in England's second tier.
Wakefield were crowned Super League champions for the first time in the club's history with a resounding 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford, a week on from travelling to huge favourites Wigan Warriors and dispatching of them 33-6 in the semi-finals.
The success proved Wakefield's first league title for 58 years dating back to 1968, and all the more remarkable considering they were relegated from Super League in 2023, playing the 2024 season in the Championship under Powell.
"I'm just amazed really at the players and how good they've been," Powell said.
"Obviously it's pretty sweet for me as an individual but for the club, the players, the coaching staff, everything that we've built up over the last three years is phenomenal.
"We've been building for a while but the last two weeks in particular have been just incredible performances from an unbelievable group of players.
"The boys have got such confidence in each other, that if we all do our jobs then we can do anything we want. We've done that this year. It's just immense.
"It's been an amazing finish to the season, wow. I couldn't speak more highly of the boys about everything they do, really.
"I know there's quite a few boys in there who just can't believe it. That we've been able to do all that.
"But it's just a testament to how good they are. I'm so proud of everything. The club, the fans - the way that they've been - obviously the players. They are just such a pleasure to coach and be around. It makes it an easy job."
For Powell, 61, it was his first time leading a side out in a Super League Grand Final since 2017, when he was Castleford Tigers head coach and lost heavily to Leeds Rhinos.
Saturday's success was made even sweeter for Powell by the fact it came against Warrington, where he coached for two seasons before being dismissed in 2023.
"This is the best [achievement], really," he added. "It looked like maybe I'd slip through my career and not win the big game after 2017 and it's been a long time.
"I had a tough time at Warrington, and then to come back and do this with Wakefield, it's phenomenal.
"For me, it's right up there. Just being at Wakefield and feeling at home again in a place and being able to get a group of men together who can do special things, it's unbelievable.
"I've had some great times in my coaching career, but this is the best."
'I felt this year might be one too early - but this club can go anywhere'
Backed by an outspoken and ambitious owner in Matt Ellis, Powell admits clinching the Super League title this year was even beyond his own wild expectations and hopes.
He now believes his team and the club can kick on even more.
"This club can do anything, really," he says.
"I felt like this year might be one year too early for us but the boys have proven me wrong.
"I felt like next year, maybe. I'm so pleased for the players, you can't write that stuff, can you? It's unbelievable.
"You don't know when you're going to have another chance at this sort of stuff. I feel there's a lot of love in this team and group.
"It's kind of a bit soppy at times, but wow, what a group of men. I'm so proud to be associated with them.
"It shows special things can be achieved.
"Some other clubs have done great things, maybe at different timescales, but this is an unbelievable story. From me thinking a bloke was trying to sell me a kitchen [owner Matt Ellis] to winning the Super League trophy. It's been an unbelievable three years."
Jowitt: A rollercoaster of a year for me - highs are worth the lows
Wakefield's Max Jowitt to Sky Sports:
"A million per cent the highs are worth the lows.
"It didn't feel real that we were playing a Grand Final until we got here today.
"A rollercoaster of a year for me personally after dropping down to the reserves, not finding form, but I got my opportunity at the back end of the year.
"For this to be my last game for Wakefield, I will never forget it."
'Emotional' Johnstone: I can't believe it - my dream for the last decade!
Rob Burrow Award winner Tom Johnstone to Sky Sports:
"I can't quite believe it. I keep crying, I can't help myself! Such a special club, it's been the longest week of my life.
"To get out there and get it done, I don't know what to say.
"This club means eveyrthing to me. I've been saying it for a long time. My dream the last 10 years was to win a Grand Final with Wakefield.
"Daryl Powell sold me the dream that we were a club that had aspirations and wanted to win things.
"I believed every word they said and this is where we are now.
"We don't do this without that belief we have. We built our foundation on that."

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she was told during her talks with U.S. President Donald Trump in New York last month that U.S. trade is suffering due to the weakness of the yen.
“At the Japan-U.S. leadership meeting, they spoke of the difficulties American trade is facing due to the weak yen, to which I responded that as a rule of thumb an undervalued yen is a problem,” Takaichi said in an exclusive interview with broadcaster NTV. She was responding to a question over whether the U.S. and Japan are aligned on tackling the weakness of the currency.
Takaichi added that in conversations with Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had indicated he understood the Japanese government’s economic policy and had not made any requests regarding its direction.
“There’s no change to my thinking that we will continue to pursue a strong economy and sustainable government finances based on responsible and proactive fiscal policy,” she said in the interview broadcast Thursday evening.
The Trump administration has been unusually vocal in expressing its concern over the weak yen. Bessent has repeatedly suggested the Bank of Japan should raise interest rates to help the yen find an appropriate level. In a speech at a university in Texas, he said he had “pretty good insight” into what Japanese policymakers were going to do and even dared speculators to bet against him.
Japanese officials have generally played down the influence of the U.S. comments on policymaking.
Tokyo and Washington conducted a joint intervention in currency markets after the yen started trading around ¥164 against the dollar. The move was their first joint action to prop up the yen in 28 years. At the time, Trump described the intervention as a sign of friendship.
Takaichi’s comments suggest addressing concerns that Japanese exporters are benefiting from a weak yen is another incentive for Washington to back Tokyo.
In the interview, Takaichi avoided making any specific comments on currency markets and spoke instead of her vision for economic revitalization that would support the yen.
“We are seeking to raise Japan’s potential growth rate and strengthen its supply capabilities through bold investments in risk management and growth, in order to achieve a strong economy,” she said. “I believe increasing the competitiveness of Japan’s economy will ultimately lead to trust in the yen.”

Jerry Golod, the producer of “Tales From the Darkside,” died following a brief battle with cancer at his home in Rancho Mirage, Calif., on Wednesday. He was 87.
Throughout his career, Golod served as an executive at CBS and NBC, later launching JayGee Productions in the early 1980s. After seeing the success of Stephen King’s 1982 film “Creepshow,” Golod collaborated with director Romero and producer Richard P. Rubinstein to bring the narrative to television. The three of them went on to launch “Tales From the Darkside,” which ran for four seasons and garnered a high cult following.
He also helped launch “Adderly” after reading Elliott Baker’s 1971 book, “Pocock and Pitt,” and becoming intrigued by the secondary character of the same name. The adventure series starred Winston Rekert and ran for two seasons on CBS.
Popular on Variety
In 1975, Golod became vice president of children’s programs at CBS before moving to NBC Entertainment in 1979 as vice president and national program director. While there, he oversaw daytime and children’s programming, specials, variety and West Coast late-night programming. He later joined CBS Television Studios and The CW in developing a new revival of “Tales From the Darkside,” though the series never moved past a 2015 pilot.
Golod executive produced CBS’s “Brass” in 1985 and “Return to Green Acres,” which reunited cast members of the 1960s sitcom. He also executive produced the 1991 revival of “Land of the Lost,” which ran for two seasons.
Golod was born in the Bronx on Dec. 26, 1938, and graduated from City College of New York. He began his career at advertising agency Dancer Fitzgerald Sample and went on to become vice president and associate director of programming. He also spent three years overseeing a television production company affiliated with the agency.
In the ‘90s, Golod worked with Pet Television Network as co-chairman and co-owner of a cable and satellite service aimed toward animal enthusiasts.
Golod is survived by his wife of 59 years, Ruth; their children, Dori and Jason; son-in-law Doug; daughter-in-law Danielle; grandchildren Gavin, Ramey, Morgan and Madison; great-grandsons Everett and Winslow; and nieces and nephews Jill, David, Elise, Renee, Celia, Ari and Ava.

Just short of its 200th birthday, a landmark natural history museum shuts down
PHILADELPHIA — Every weekend for the past month, the sidewalk in front of the Natural Academy of Sciences has simultaneously felt like a festival, a funeral, and a science fair.
On the Museum's final Friday, there was a line of attendees waiting to get in; Activists circulating petitions and flyers to "Save the Academy"; and a museum educator showed off a giant salamander skull and a rare coat of pangolin scales.
For Philly area kids, visiting this place has been a rite of passage for generations. So when word dropped on September 1st that the nearly 200-year-old museum was closing at the end of the month, thousands of families began a wistful pilgrimage, to make one final visit.
"This is a very special place, for my family and also me growing up," said Alexandria McCormick, who was visiting with her husband and six kids. She said when she was a child, her family used to come multiple times a year, awakening her love of natural history.
"It makes me really sad to think that my children might not also grow up having these experiences and being inspired to love nature this way." she said.
Founded in 1812, and opened to the public in 1828, the Academy of Natural Sciences was the first place in the world to display a dinosaur skeleton, back in 1868. There's also mammal dioramas, live animals, and other rotating exhibits.
Its collection of scientific specimens is widely recognized as one of the most important in the world. And its sudden demise comes amidst a continuing decline in funding for cultural and scientific institutions.
"This is the oldest natural history museum in the Americas," says Isa Betancourt, who worked in the Academy's entomology department for 10 years, from 2011 to 2021.
Betancourt now lives in Arizona, but hopped on a plane and came back to Philly to help organize the "Save the Academy" campaign, which included a flurry of rallies, marches, and an online petition to keep the museum open that has over 114,000 signatures.
"If this museum can slip away like that, what's stopping other museums from going the same way? We can't let this be a precedent." she added.
A sudden closure
Drexel University, which took over financial responsibility for the Academy in 2011, explained on its website that post-pandemic, costs have risen and attendance declined. In its last few weeks, however, museum attendance skyrocketed and revenue was more than 20 times higher than last September.
"Maybe if they had announced this last year, they could have gotten the crowds they have now," said Zoe Abrams, who was visiting with her husband and two children. "This is busier than Grand Central. Could have saved things."
Some people working to save it criticized Drexel for not participating in any efforts to stem the museums' closure, or providing details about how much it would cost to keep it open.
"When they announced the one month notice it was a surprise for everybody," said Betancourt. "It's like the leadership didn't even try to keep it open, and that's why there's a lot of frustration around what's happening. It's just not right." she added.
In response to a request for comment, Drexel said in a statement that it "remains deeply committed to protecting the Academy of Natural Sciences' extraordinary legacy."
Less than a week before the September 30th closing date, the William Penn Foundation offered a year's worth of bridge funding; to buy time to explore more permanent solutions. Drexel said it is exploring the possibility of working with the foundation, but would need a plan for long-term sustainability before considering re-opening the museum.
Hard times for scientific institutions
The Academy houses a massive, irreplaceable library of over 19 million specimens. It includes Thomas Jefferson's fossil collection, and plant samples gathered by Lewis and Clark. It also has an archive of 73,000 holotype specimens— carefully preserved samples which scientists use as references for defining and naming species.
Drexel has said it will preserve access to that collection for students and researchers. But it's unclear what that means for the general public. And all this uncertainty comes at a moment when government support for cultural institutions has been in steep decline. "It's certainly a challenging time for the museum field." said Natanya Kashan, a spokesperson for the American Alliance of Museums. A 2025 survey of AAM's members found a third had government grants and contracts cancelled, and more than two-thirds were affected by executive orders in some way."The financial pressures are not only in federal funding, they're also in philanthropy, in corporate donations, in individual giving," she said.
The Academy tied its financial fate to Drexel's, when, in 2011, the two institutions announced an "affiliation." The Academy became a subsidiary of Drexel, but retained its own board and 501c3 organizational status. In a statement announcing the partnership the Academy's president bragged about "a rock-solid balance sheet with a $51 million endowment".
But, like many Universities, Drexel has been struggling financially, in part due to declining enrollment. In 2024, the school reported it was facing a budget shortfall.
And as attendance shrank, in 2025 the museum laid off some staff, and reduced its hours. It soon cancelled its 2026 summer camp program. Earlier this year, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported that the university and the Academy were renegotiating heir relationship; Drexel wanted a full merger, which would grant it the building, endowment and collections.
Amid speculation that Drexel plans to sell the 150-year-old building housing the Academy, Philadelphia's city council proposed altering local zoning overlays in order to make selling the building or converting it to other uses more difficult. The council also plans to hold special public hearings, to find out how the Academy got to the point of closing, and what possible solutions might look like. The legislation calling for the hearing also gives the council subpoena power over Drexel.
"We need to know how this came to be. What were the levers that created this decision, and how do we undo that decision?" said City councilmember Dr. Nina Ahmad.
"There was no campaign in the recent past that we can find to encourage or to tell the city of Philadelphia, 'We're in danger of closing if you don't come and use our museum.' None of that."
Philadelphia does have a track record of saving financially struggling cultural institutions, including the renowned Art collection at The Barnes Foundation, and the Please Touch Children's Museum. But those campaigns took place before their respective museums closed. Reopening an already shuttered institution could be much more difficult.

Mumbai, October 3, 2026: The Maharashtra Transport Department will launch a special drive from October 5 to 17 to identify private vehicles registered in other states but being used regularly in Maharashtra for more than a year.
The move comes amid concerns that some vehicle owners may be registering their vehicles outside Maharashtra to avoid paying the higher motor vehicle tax applicable in the state.
Transport Commissioner Rajesh Narwekar has directed all Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) and Deputy RTOs to carry out the verification. Vehicles found to have been used in Maharashtra beyond the permissible period without completing the required formalities may face action, including detention, re-registration and recovery of motor vehicle tax.
Rules For Out-Of-State Vehicles
Under Section 47 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a vehicle registered in one state can be used in another state for up to 12 months. If it is to be kept and used in the new state beyond that period, the owner is required to apply for re-registration and pay the applicable motor vehicle tax.
Maharashtra Motor Vehicle Rules also require information to be submitted to the registration authority within seven days of bringing the vehicle into the state.
During the drive, RTO officials will examine documents and other objective evidence to establish how long an out-of-state vehicle has been operating in Maharashtra.
Enforcement teams, flying squads, check posts and joint teams will be deployed at locations where such vehicles are likely to be found, including metropolitan areas, industrial zones, commercial and residential complexes and large parking facilities.
The department has also directed officials to record details of vehicles checked, violations detected, action taken, vehicles detained and tax recovered on a daily basis through a Google Sheet. A consolidated compliance report will be submitted to the Transport Commissioner after the drive.
Focus On 5,664 High-Value Vehicles
The special drive assumes significance as the department is separately examining 5,664 high-value vehicles that were sold by dealers in Maharashtra during 2025-26 but subsequently registered outside the state.
The vehicles, each valued at more than Rs 50 lakh, include luxury and sports cars as well as cranes, trucks and excavators. RTO officials have been asked to verify the registration documents, owners' addresses and reasons for registering the vehicles outside Maharashtra.
According to officials, several vehicles were registered in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, where lower taxation could be one of the reasons for out-of-state registration.
Officials are also examining cranes and excavators, for which the tax structure has shifted from weight-based assessment to taxation based on vehicle value.
The department has not, however, concluded that these vehicles were illegally registered or that their owners deliberately evaded tax.
The 5,664 vehicles are valued between Rs 50 lakh and Rs 3 crore. If the minimum value of Rs 50 lakh is considered for each vehicle, their combined value comes to around Rs 28,320 crore. Preliminary calculations indicate that the potential tax involved could run into hundreds of crores.
The department has estimated that Maharashtra could have earned between Rs 2,500 crore and Rs 3,000 crore if the vehicles had been registered in the state. The actual revenue impact will depend on the verification.
Three to four senior motor vehicle inspectors have been assigned in the concerned RTO jurisdictions. They will verify whether address documents submitted for Certificates of Registration of Temporary Registration (CRTeM) complied with Rule 4 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.
The nine RTOs that issued the temporary registration certificates have been asked to provide the relevant documents. The RTO-wise figures include Thane with 1,272 certificates, Pimpri-Chinchwad with 1,061, Wadala with 754, Navi Mumbai with 617, Panvel with 571 and Nagpur with 387.
Owners Can Shift Registration
For owners who have genuinely shifted to Maharashtra, the process is different from cases where vehicles are allegedly kept outside the state only to save tax.
Transport expert MD Faizal said the department should focus on vehicles where there is evidence of deliberate tax avoidance rather than penalising people who move to Maharashtra for work or studies for a few years.
“If a person has shifted to Maharashtra for work or studies, keeping the vehicle in the home state may serve little purpose,” he said, stressing the need to distinguish such cases from intentional tax avoidance.
After 12 months, an owner who intends to permanently keep the vehicle in Maharashtra generally has to obtain an NOC from the original RTO, along with the required documents and police clearance.
The vehicle is then inspected by the Maharashtra RTO before Forms 20 and 27, the original RC, insurance, PUC and Maharashtra address proof are submitted.
The owner must also pay the applicable pro-rata Maharashtra road tax. After re-registration, the owner can seek a refund of the unused portion of the lifetime tax paid in the original state.
For vehicles registered outside Maharashtra, owners may also have to approach the authorised manufacturer or dealer for HSRP installation, as required.
RTO officials said vehicle owners should approach the concerned manufacturer or dealership to obtain the required high-security registration plate.

Coast Guard searching for missing medical plane carrying 6 people
The U.S. Coast Guard is searching the waters south of Nantucket, Mass., for a Canadian air ambulance that disappeared early Saturday while traveling from Bermuda to Boston.
The Gulfstream G100 is believed to have been carrying six people on board when it lost contact with air traffic control, according to the Coast Guard.
Flight data shows the jet dropped at least 9,000 feet over two minutes, then leveled off for several more minutes, before disappearing. The pilot declared an emergency, according to Nantucket Memorial Airport. During an exchange, air traffic control asked the pilot of the air ambulance, "You're coming in blind?"
A fire rescue dispatcher warned emergency crews to prepare for the planes' arrival. She said it was 15 minutes away, suffering from electrical issues and had lost radio and radar, according to audio on Broadcastify and reviewed by The Boston Globe.
The Coast Guard has deployed two search and rescue planes as well as a helicopter and a motor lifeboat.
The plane is operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, based in Ontario, Canada. The company website says it has run thousands of missions since 2009 returning patients and loved ones to their families back home. The firm boasts "a flawless safety record."
The website says the air ambulances are staffed by two pilots and a medical team and include a stretcher as well as full ICU medical equipment and supplies.

The central government released a draft ordinance Saturday laying out requirements for designating “secondary capitals” that would serve as substitutes for Tokyo in the event of a major disaster.
Sapporo, Nagoya, Osaka and Fukuoka — the capital cities of Hokkaido, Aichi Prefecture, Osaka Prefecture, and Fukuoka Prefecture, respectively — all met the proposed criteria, according to NHK.
The four prefectures have expressed their intention to apply for secondary capital designation to the central government.
The government began soliciting public comments on the draft ordinance the same day, planning to finalize it later this month.
Under the draft ordinance, prefectures that are considered unlikely to suffer damage at the same time as the Tokyo metropolitan area would be eligible, excluding areas that would be affected by a possible major earthquake directly beneath Tokyo or an eruption of Mount Fuji.
Eligible prefectures must also meet the following requirements: contain a city with at least 14 regional offices of central government agencies; have an ordinance-designated major city whose population accounts for at least 1.2% of the country’s total population; have an economic scale that accounts for at least 2.1% of Japan’s gross domestic product; and have an ordinance-designated city that is reorganized into a special ward or concludes a partnership agreement with the prefectural government.
The four prefectures already meet the first three requirements and can apply for secondary capital designation after meeting the fourth.
A secondary capital is aimed at creating a multipolar and decentralized economic zone by developing alternative functions for the country’s capital in local areas in preparation for large-scale disasters. The designated areas are expected to implement measures such as developing alternative functions, providing tax incentives to attract private investment and introducing deregulation.
The government plans to announce its basic stance on secondary capital designation in November and outline a schedule for submitting applications.

Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami
- Published
As Nigeria begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign, former international Segun Odegbami, who won the tournament on home soil in 1980, says the country is experiencing the "worst time" in its football history.
Over the past 12 months both the Super Eagles and Super Falcons failed to qualify for their respective Fifa World Cups.
But beyond the failure of the senior national teams, Nigeria has also endured disappointing results at age-group level and in African club competitions - although the West Africans recently reached the quarter-finals of the Under-20 Women's World Cup.
Odegbami says the diminishing returns represent a "tectonic shift" for one of the continent's traditional powers.
"It has never been this bad in our entire history that we didn't qualify for the World Cup," the 74-year-old told BBC Sport Africa.
"Our girls (the Super Falcons), who were African champions, failed to win a competition (the 2025 Women's Afcon) that was just there for their taking. All our junior teams are not doing well.
"Our local league is not bringing in money. Something is definitely wrong."
The crisis has already triggered major changes within the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).
Its president Ibrahim Gusau, general secretary Mohammed Sanusi and multiple members of the federation's executive committee resigned last month following mounting criticism.
Odegbami says Nigerian football had not been represented by its "first XI administrators" and has called for a restructure to create the conditions for long-term development.
"The outcry by Nigerians was total. Everybody wanted them out, to the extent that the President of the country himself (Bola Tinubu) made the pronouncement that he wanted reforms," he said.
"Everything came together like a jigsaw puzzle and is working now for us to produce a blueprint that will cover every aspect of our football development."
- 'Motherhood should not be the end of anyone's story' 
  - Published23 July
Sweeping changes at the NFF
A joint delegation from world governing body Fifa and the Confederation of African Football (Caf) has been involved in discussions with the National Sports Commission (NSC) over the future structure of Nigerian football.
The parties are working towards a roadmap for comprehensive reforms but NFF elections, scheduled for 27 September, have been suspended.
President Tinubu stated his desire for reform to overcome what he called "repeated failures".
Emmanuel Ikpeme has been appointed NFF interim general secretary, with Ademola Olajire the interim deputy general secretary.
The changes have prompted renewed debate among stakeholders over whether the country needs a deeper restructuring.
Nigerian sports journalist Fisayo Dairo believes any reform must extend beyond a change in leadership.
"The reform should be the setting up of a proper framework and structure that our football can thrive on," Dairo told BBC Sport Africa.
"[We need to] develop national teams, harness talent from the grassroots and have governance that incorporates all forms of stakeholders.
"The corporate world has to be fully represented so that the administration is able to generate funds."
'What is Nigeria's football style?'
For Odegbami, the current situation is a stark contrast to the era in which he helped transform the Nigerian game.
Nicknamed 'Mathematical' for his precision and skill on the ball, the forward was part of the Super Eagles side that won the country's first continental title in 1980, beating Algeria 3-0 in the final in Lagos.
"We had unprecedented support and fortunately the stars aligned with us," he said.
"It was an indescribable atmosphere during that period.
"That experience you can't even describe and compare. [It remains] indelible in our minds."
Nigeria lifted the Afcon trophy again in 1994 and 2013, and finished as runners-up at the 2023 edition.
The team also finished third in 2019 and at this year's finals in Morocco.
However, Odegbami argues sport has "not been a priority" of successive governments and believes his nation has been failed by football administrators since the mid 1990s.
"The pilots are not guiding us well, they haven't guided us well," he said.
"And that has affected every aspect of our football development: the grassroots, the discovery of players, the development of the players, the establishment of the institutions that will take care of them, the academies, the clubs that they will go into both locally and internationally.
"What is the coaching methodology? What is the philosophy of our football in the country?
"What is our culture, what is our style?"
Decaying infrastructure
Yet, alongside the failure to reach the past two men's World Cups, concerns over deteriorating infrastructure and inadequate investment have become recurring themes in discussions about the state of the Nigerian game.
Across Africa, meanwhile, other nations have continued to invest in hosting major competitions.
Senegal will be the venue for the Youth Olympic Games next month, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia are holding next year's men's Cricket World Cup, Kenya will stage the 2029 World Athletics Championship, and Morocco will co-host the 2030 World Cup with Spain and Portugal.
Odegbami has bemoaned the fact that top-class stadiums which Nigeria used to possess have fallen into disrepair after being neglected.
He name-checked the National Stadium in Surulere, Lagos, which hosted games during the 1980 and 2000 Afcons, the Liberty Stadium (now Obafemi Awolowo Stadium) in Ibadan, Kaduna's Ahmadu Bello Stadium and the UJ Esuene Stadium in Calabar.
"I weep when I think of the amount of damage they have done to Nigerian football - the infrastructure that we had in the country, some of the historic monuments that were facilities for football in this country," he said.
"Whether it was wilful, whether it was ignorance, they did irreparable damage to what was Nigeria's heritage.
"Uyo is the best we have in Nigeria, but it is not half as good as what we had from the 1960s to the 90s."
The Super Eagles will begin their Afcon 2027 qualifying campaign against Madagascar at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo on Friday (16:00 GMT) before travelling to Guinea-Bissau on 29 September.

India's influential Gen Z-led "cockroach" protesters are set to get back on the streets - this time seeking electoral reforms and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voter rolls.
A pressure group which began as an online satirical movement, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) recorded its first major victory in July when it forced education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign after weeks of protests calling for education reforms.
The CJP leaders have now called upon their supporters to gather at the sprawling Shivaji Park grounds in Mumbai city at 4pm local time (10:30 GMT) on Friday "to save democracy" and seek CEC Kumar's resignation.

The differences were reported to be mostly over a controversial revision of the country's electoral rolls known as the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, which began last year.

Last week's Indian Express report said the two commissioners had also been raising questions over the integrity of the voter database, changes to the way new voters are enrolled and the security of the electoral rolls itself.

But the revelations sparked a furore, with opposition leaders demanding Kumar's resignation.
Leader of the opposition and senior Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi has repeatedly accused the commission of "stealing votes from the opposition" and said those officers who were indulging in "vote theft" were "traitors".
Another senior opposition leader, Mamata Banerjee, has demanded the CEC's arrest.
On Wednesday, the INDIA alliance - an opposition grouping that includes nearly two dozen parties and has both Gandhi and Banerjee as members - said they would also organise protest rallies across the country in the coming days. On 6 October, all opposition MPs plan to march to the Election Commission office in Delhi, they added.
Many of the opposition parties have also pledged support to the protest in Mumbai.
Despite Mumbai police denying them permission to hold the protest, Dipke has insisted that they will assemble and if the police arrest them, they will launch a "Jail Bharo Andolan (fill the prison movement)".
In a short animation video posted on its social media accounts on Wednesday, the CJP said it was a citizen's right to be able to vote and to not allow an eligible voter to cast their vote was an "issue of serious concern in a democracy".
"We demand transparency and accountability from the commission and want the CEC to resign. This is not a fight for one party, it's for free and fair elections and every citizen's right to vote," it added.

Bangkok is used to absorbing the sudden afternoon downpours that inundate the city during the rainy season. Even streets in many central high-rise districts can briefly turn into rivers, with rats and cockroaches racing out of sewers and taking temporary refuge on trees and buildings as the subterranean world is flushed out.
But every city has a breaking point, and this year rain fell so fast and so hard that whole neighbourhoods of the Thai capital have been transformed, not into rivers, but stagnant lakes. In parts of the city, roughly 300mm of rain – the equivalent of half a year of average rainfall in London – fell in about two days.
About 40 people died in flood-related incidents, according to the government. A number of the deaths were from drowning and several from accidental electrocution. Thousands of people stayed in more than 230 shelters across the city, authorities said.
Suleemas Kurangkul, a 73-year-old resident of a block of flats whose ground floor stairs are still under water, said last weekend’s rain was not the usual evening storm but was constant, “like all day, all night”.
“The water just kept rising,” said Suleemas, whose flat is above the waterline on the second floor. By the time she and her neighbours received a mobile phone warning, it was too late, and the street-level water was waist-high.
The 1970s Khlong Chan flat compound in north-east Bangkok where Suleemas lives has become a symbol of the disaster. Photos have been shared across Thailand of the flats rising out of the brownish water, with the rooftops of parked cars barely peeking above the surface, although the authorities had managed to drain away the worst of it by Thursday.
Later in the week, during a brief respite in the rain, Suleemas said the water had receded somewhat. “People are so happy to see the sunshine,” she said. “Yet, the smell is getting stronger. So much debris and rubbish floating all over the place.”
Built on a vast floodplain of the Chao Phraya River, Bangkok, a megacity of millions, relies on a network of muddy canals to drain water, as well as pumps and dikes. But concrete construction has destroyed much of the canal network, and the city is unable to cope.
The government has declared a flood disaster across all 50 of the city’s districts. Some neighbourhoods have turned into dystopian scenes, with people using blow-up paddling pools or, in one case, a floating fridge, as boats to reach their homes. One man was arrested for riding a jetski along a main road.
“It’s a lesson,” said Chaleerat Chamrasporn, 55, a resident. “The kids are into doomsday-themed content, so now they can see what the ‘end of the world’ is actually like, or rather, that this is just the beginning.”
Flooding has also disrupted Bangkok’s main Suvarnabhumi airport, with about half of Thai Airways’ workforce unable to report for work at one point this week, causing thousands of items of luggage to pile up and forcing flight cancellations. Many schools have closed, and with much of the capital in gridlock even people in less affected areas have been stuck at home.
Thailand’s prime minister, Anutin Charnvirakul, told reporters that Bangkok’s metropolitan area was still at risk from flood waters flowing in from the north, and said a war room had been set up to monitor the situation. Thailand’s weather agency has forecast more heavy rain for next week.
It is part of a pattern that seems to be setting in this part of the world. South-east Asia has already seen a worsening of extreme floods, scientists say, a trend that is set to worsen as fossil fuel pollutants bake the planet further. Hot seas evaporate more water and warm air can hold more moisture, allowing downpours to crash down with far more force.
“In central Thailand, I can see from my maps, we have already seen a small but significant trend towards extreme rainfall,” said Nikolaos Skliris, an ocean scientist at the University of Southampton who has studied heavy rain in the region. “In the long-term, all models show this will be amplified – more rainfall, and more extreme rainfall.”
It is too early for scientists to attribute these particular rains to climate breakdown without doing a study. They were caused by a low-pressure system that moved from an unusually warm South China Sea over Cambodia and Vietnam before getting stuck above Bangkok, which was fairly cool, data from Copernicus Climate Pulse showed.
The picture is complicated by the emergence of an abnormally strong El Niño, a cyclical weather pattern that brings record heat and more violent extremes around the world. Its presence typically leads to drier summer conditions in south-east Asia but recent research suggests it still exacerbates days with extreme rainfall.
Naim Laeni, a consultant and part-time university lecturer who co-authored a study on Bangkok’s flood resilience, said authorities had underestimated the strength of the rains, which persisted for days. The city’s drainage canals can handle about 60mm of rain an hour, rising to 80mm in upgraded sections, but localised bursts exceeded this while leaving too little time between periods of stress.
“The government did not communicate the seriousness,” said Laeni. “Usually in Bangkok we receive heavy rain for a few hours, not for days.”
Neighbouring Myanmar has suffered from the same weather system, with flash floods and blocked roads complicating rescue efforts in the country.
Rescuers were pulling bodies from a landslide that devastated the village of Ka Det Nge Htein in Myanmar’s south at the weekend. That disaster had already claimed nine lives, and eight more people are missing under the mud in another village, local officials said.
Civil war across the country, and a junta that restricts the media, have made it hard to get information, and hampered aid organisations.
Back in Bangkok, pumping stations have been operating at full capacity, but it could be days before the waters fully drain.
At her apartment complex, Suleemas said she would stay where she was with her neighbours.
“It’s hard, yes, very hard,” she said. “But together we are fighting and biting through it. When we get together to help one another like this, our spirit can keep us on our feet; we can get through it all together.”
Agence France-Presse contributed to this report
