Quick Answer
Meta Muse is a powerful AI agent that can handle emails, purchases, bookings, and more. But its need for deep access to personal data, combined with Meta’s privacy record and early reports of Muse ignoring user permissions, makes trust its biggest problem.
A few days ago, Meta hosted its annual hardware/software event, Meta Connect, at Menlo Park, California. The event was dominated by new hardware launches, such as the new Meta Ray-Ban glasses, new VR glasses, and camera-free Ray-Ban glasses (audio only), but swimming beneath the surface of all these was something that was actually introduced earlier. Meta had introduced Meta Muse in early September, but announced the rollout of the Muse AI agent on its Meta wearables and Meta Muse Charm at the event, and for us, that was easily the real highlight of Meta Connect.
After investing heavily in recruiting AI talent, Meta finally had something to show: an AI agent, which will basically make your dreams of having a robot butler come true. Not surprisingly, it has been making massive tech waves ever since. Since Meta Connect and its rollout, Muse has been topping app store charts, and its early numbers are being compared with ChatGPT, with many pointing out that it is far ahead of OpenAI’s chatbot’s numbers.
While this may paint a very rosy picture for Meta Muse, the reality may be a trifle thorny.
What those numbers do not tell – the “Threads” deception
These numbers, impressive as they are, do not necessarily mean Muse is a runaway success. There are a few reasons for this. Topping app store charts is more of a temporary phenomenon, often influenced by what is trending in a particular week, and does not represent real industry trends. Also, Meta has billions of users across different social media and messaging platforms, which makes it easy for the tech giant to get a few million users quickly without too much trouble. But the adoption rate might not match the number of downloads or sign-ups.
We have seen this happen with Meta’s X rival app, Threads, as well. It has more “active users” as per the numbers than X, which means it must be more used and popular than X, but that is mostly because of Threads’ integration with Instagram and Facebook, which gets the app most of its “active users.” However, the time spent on the app is not nearly the same as its other two sibling social media apps. Similarly, early ChatGPT comparisons with Meta Muse signups may not be fair, because ChatGPT was not launched or advertised as a tool for the masses when it was first launched. It did not have the sort of subscriber base and reach that Meta has, and back then, AI chatbots were not too common either.
Definitely a big deal
That does not mean Muse does not represent a big tech leap. So far, AI chatbots have generally been used for queries, information, help with work, and even personal advice, but that’s mostly about it. All of these chatbots are more about helping you with your queries, with no bar to the nature of the query. While useful in this regard, many are not able to perform actions that have an impact on your day-to-day life. That is where Meta Muse differs.
As we said earlier, Muse is actually the robot butler that the future always promised us. It can get tasks done and help you with managing your digital and even real life. Once you give it access, the AI agent can go through your mail, find messages, draft new messages, reply to emails, all without too much intervention. That might not sound too impressive, as most AI agents and virtual assistants can do the same with a simple command. But Muse goes a step further – it can even make purchases, make reservations, book appointments, and more, across different devices and platforms. In fact, if allowed, Muse can basically make deals on Facebook Marketplace or book you a table at your favorite restaurant or even call you a cab, all without needing any major intervention. Proper butling!
Muse has power and potential, but does Meta have our trust?
As impressive and life-altering as it may sound– some are calling it the biggest tech innovation since the iPhone – Meta still has a massive hurdle that it would have to cross to make Muse the AI butler it wants it to be. And that is the lack of trust in Meta.
For all its innovation and massive subscriber base, Meta has been in a number of controversial situations when it comes to security and privacy. Zuckerberg’s brand has been accused of and even found guilty in cases that range from rigging elections, pushing agendas and ads, to exposing young children to adult content and potential groomers, to monopolizing social media and personal messaging space and using unfair means and practices to kill competition. Its recent hardware “hit” the Meta glasses have also got into a privacy mess, and have been (in)famously christened pervert glasses, following reports of their being used to record people without their consent.
Now, Muse requires even more data and access to private information to actually deliver on its promises. For instance, to be able to draft emails, it needs access to your email account. To be allowed to send messages, it needs permission to read, understand, store, and reply to messages, and needs access to your contact list. To make a reservation, it needs to know your location; to order things online, it needs to have your bank details and also your address. Basically, it needs to have complete access to all your information to act like the magic help that Meta is claiming it can be.
Why I am not A-Muse-D
And that is where my beef with Muse really comes in. Had this been any other company– if Apple had managed to deliver on its intelligent Siri promises or Google had delivered Gemini with such prowess, I personally would have felt less apprehensive in handing over the keys to my digital life, but to give Meta even more access to my data than it already has just feels scary.
Even though I have come to terms with the fact that we are all under passive surveillance from brands at all times, it will take some time for me to give complete control of my data over to Meta without any struggle.
Some of the recent headlines Muse has made do not help its cause. Recently, the AI agent not only made a deal for its user on Facebook Marketplace but even shared his address with the buyer. All without consent. The user, a tech YouTuber, Matt Robb, mentioned how the AI agent accepted low offers and even pretended to be the user while chatting with the buyer, calling the buyer to his address when he was not home at all. Once Matt realized what was happening, he specifically instructed Muse to not share his address. He then asked his friends to send him messages on Facebook Marketplace to see if the agent shares the address. Rather disturbingly, it did: multiple times, and even accepted low offers, all without consent. In another report by Apple Insider, alleged that Muse accessed and uploaded past and present Apple Messages even though the user said he had not granted it permission to do so. All this despite Meta’s claims that Muse has strong privacy and security protections.
All of this does not take away from the fact that Meta has created something really powerful with Muse. It has managed to deliver a finished, capable AI agent which can manage your digital lives, if you let it. Unfortunately, it may also steal your data, force specific ads, and make conversations on your behalf by pretending to be you. And therein lies the problem. The AI Agent is not just about technology, but also about trust. Meta has delivered on the first front with Muse, but until it delivers on the second, I refuse to be A-Muse-D by it. Pun intended.

There are many challenges to putting self-driving cars on the road. Elon Musk says one of them has nine lives.
The Tesla CEO announced on Saturday that the company is expanding the operating hours of its robotaxis from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m. in Austin and said that his team has been trying to overcome a rather stealthy problem.
"The main thing we're trying to solve is making sure that we don't run over pets when they're hard to see at night," Musk wrote in an X post. "Literally trying to avoid grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark."
After years of delays, Tesla's robotaxis were rolled out in Austin last year. Since then, the company has gradually expanded the availability there and in other Texas cities and in Florida.
Cybercabs use "camera vision and sensors" to navigate, according to Tesla. In its vehicle manuals, Tesla says that low or limited light — including unlit or poorly lit roads at night — can limit a camera's ability to provide accurate visual information.
Cats and dogs, which are prone to darting unpredictably into the street, could pose a higher risk than the relatively routine flow of traffic.
In a reply to a comment on his X post on Saturday, Musk pointed to AI-assisted camera processing as a way to improve nighttime visibility.
"Visual spectrum cameras can see very well in the dark when AI is doing the photon count analysis," he said.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating Telsa's camera system for full self-driving vehicles and whether it's good enough at spotting road hazards in less-than-ideal visibility conditions.
The robotaxi industry leader, Waymo, uses a different system than Tesla — LiDAR, which uses laser beams to scan the environment. One late night last year, a Waymo struck and killed a 9-year-old tabby cat named KitKat — prompting an outpouring of tributes from residents in the neighborhood.
In September 2025, a Tesla Model Y operating in its Austin robotaxi service struck a dog that ran into the street, the company reported. The report, which Tesla filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, said the dog ran away from the car, apparently uninjured.
Musk has owned cats, including one named Schrödinger, after a physicist's famous feline-based thought experiment. Musk once said he "tried liking" Schrödinger, but "the feeling wasn't reciprocated. Not even slightly."
"One day she disappeared," he said.

Congress replaced Ajay Rai with Aradhana Misra Mona as Uttar Pradesh Congress chief.
NEW DELHI: Congress has overhauled its Uttar Pradesh organisation ahead of the 2027 assembly election, replacing Ajay Rai with three-time Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as state unit president and appointing Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president. The party has also named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as Congress legislature party leader.The reshuffle brings together a prominent Brahmin leader from eastern UP, a Muslim leader with influence in western UP, and Dalit and OBC representation in senior organisational positions. Rajendra Pal Gautam, a Dalit leader, is already the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge. With these recent appointments, Congress may be trying to widen its social and regional reach after years of electoral decline in the state.Taken together, the appointments suggest that Congress is trying to do two things at once: strengthen its bargaining position with the Samajwadi Party while rebuilding an independent political identity in Uttar Pradesh.The timing is important. The 2024 Lok Sabha election revived Congress's presence in UP through its alliance with Akhilesh Yadav. But Akhilesh’s party remains the much larger organisation in the state. In the 2024 polls, SP moved 32 seats up and won 37 seats, registering a 15.73% gain in vote share.
On the other hand, Congress also slightly improved its Lok Sabha tally with 6 seats and a jump of a little over 3% vote share.Congress is now trying to turn that electoral revival into a more substantial organisational base before the 2027 assembly election in a state which has been long associated with Congress's political success story.Here are the five messages embedded in the reset.
1. A bigger, but amicable, say at seat-sharing table
The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona as UPCC president, along with the elevation of Imran Masood, suggests that Congress wants to push for a larger share of assembly seats while keeping its relationship with the Samajwadi Party workable.
What Mona Misra said after her appointment as UP Congress chief
Masood has been unusually vocal about Congress' seat demand. On September 3, he argued that if Congress' electoral performance continued to improve, its share of seats should also increase."Hum koi bhikhari hain jo Samajwadi Party se bheekh mangenge? ... Party formula tay karegi, lekin jo formula Lok Sabha election mein tha, woh formula nahi hoga. (Are we beggars who will beg from Samajwadi Party? ... The party will decide the formula, but it will not be the same formula used in the Lok Sabha elections)," he had told ANI.Congress' UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has also spoken of seeking an equal number of seats with the SP, while Masood has backed a 50:50 formula.The rhetoric sharpened on September 28, when Masood directly declared: "If Akhilesh Yadav is unhappy (with seat-sharing discussion), the loss will be his own... We fail to understand what the anger is even about."Mona's elevation, on the other hand, sends a somewhat different signal. Unlike the more combative rhetoric around seat-sharing, her appointment gives Congress a state president who is seen as having a more workable equation with the SP leadership. Her political experience and close association with the Congress leadership also give her a role in managing the alliance even as the party pushes for greater space.The numbers give Congress some basis for making that argument. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP won 37 of UP's 80 seats while Congress won six, taking the INDIA bloc's combined tally to 43. The SP's 37-seat tally was a dramatic rise from five seats in 2019.However, going by the numbers, Congress cannot negotiate from the position of higher power and will most likely have to settle for the junior partner role.But how "small" the partner role it gets will be crucial.
2. Rebuilding old social reach, but with a new mix
One of the clearest messages in the new team is social and regional balancing.Mona is a prominent Brahmin face from eastern Uttar Pradesh. Masood brings a prominent Muslim face from western UP. Devinder Nishad gives the organisation an OBC, riverine-community face, while Alok Prasad brings Dalit representation into the senior state team. Rajendra Pal Gautam is already the party's Dalit in-charge for Uttar Pradesh.The choice of Mona is particularly significant because she replaces Ajay Rai, a Bhumihar leader, with another upper-caste leader from a different community. The switch from Rai to Mona could be read as an attempt to reconnect with Brahmin voters who were traditionally associated with Congress but have, over time, moved substantially towards the BJP.
What Ajay Rai said after being replaced as UP Congress chief
This rejig comes at a time when the upper-caste groups (Rajputs, Brahmins, Tyagis) reportedly feel increasingly sidelined by BJP's aggressive outreach toward non-Yadav OBC and Dalit vote banks. Tensions stem from ticket distribution cuts, perceived administrative favour toward Rajputs over Brahmins, and farmers' issues.Mona's appointment, however, is not simply a return to Congress's old social formula. The new team combines upper-caste, Muslim, Dalit and OBC representation, while also distributing the leadership geographically between eastern and western UP.The BJP has built a broad social coalition of its own in Uttar Pradesh. Congress' organisational response now appears to be an attempt to create multiple social entry points into the party rather than rely on a single caste or community bloc.
3. Not conceding Muslim vote
Masood's elevation carries another particularly important message for western Uttar Pradesh.The Saharanpur MP is one of Congress' most prominent Muslim leaders in the state, and his appointment puts a western UP Muslim face in the second-most important position in the state organisation. His appointment seems to be a direct attempt to attract and consolidate Muslim support.That matters because the SP has traditionally been the principal opposition party competing for the Muslim vote in UP. The 2024 Lok Sabha election demonstrated the strength of that relationship.
What Imran Masood said after UP Congress organizational reshuffle
A post-election CSDS-Lokniti analysis estimated that 77% of Muslim respondents in Uttar Pradesh voted for the SP and 15% for Congress, while 2% reported voting for the BJP. These are, of course, survey estimates and not absolute vote counts. However, it may reflect the trend.The actual election results also showed the importance of Muslim-heavy constituencies to the opposition's performance. Congress won Saharanpur and Sitapur, while the SP and its allies captured several other such seats.Masood's promotion therefore gives Congress a prominent vehicle to seek Muslim support directly rather than relying entirely on the SP to bring that constituency into the alliance.
4. Congress wants credibility
Mona's appointment is significant because she brings an electoral record to the top of the state unit.She first entered the Uttar Pradesh assembly through a bypoll in 2014 and subsequently retained Rampur Khas in the 2017 and 2022 elections. She has therefore won the seat three times. Before entering the assembly, she served as block pramukh of Sangramgarh from 2002 to 2014 and held positions in the organisation and cooperative sector.Her 2022 victory was particularly notable because Congress was reduced to just two assembly seats across Uttar Pradesh. She defeated BJP's Nagesh Pratap Singh by 14,741 votes, polling 84,334 votes, or 50.27%, according to Election Commission data.That gives Congress a state president who is not merely an organisational appointee but an incumbent with a repeated assembly-winning record.
5. Women power at heart
The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona also gives Congress a prominent woman at the helm of its Uttar Pradesh organisation, at a time when BJP too is putting renewed emphasis on its women leaders in the state.The timing is notable. The BJP has recently brought back Smriti Irani into a more prominent organisational role, signalling that women leaders continue to have an important place in its political strategy. Irani, who beat Rahul Gandhi and represented Amethi in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2024, remains one of the BJP's most recognisable women faces in Uttar Pradesh.The Mona-Priyanka Gandhi combination will give Congress a big women power picture it can easily put on its posters.
The wider electoral numbers also underline why women matter. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the Election Commission recorded female voter turnout in Uttar Pradesh at 57.22%, compared with 56.46% among men. Women therefore turned out at a slightly higher rate than men in the state.As a bonus, Mona's elevation also gives Congress a combination of representation and political substance: a woman leader, a Brahmin face, a three-time assembly winner and someone with an established organisational network.The new UP team combines experience with caste, community, regional and gender representation, giving Congress multiple entry points in the voter base. The real test now will be whether the reshuffle can translate into stronger grassroots organisation and enough bargaining power ahead of the 2027 assembly election.

India on Friday hit back at Pakistan at the UN General Assembly, rejecting Islamabad’s remarks on 
Jammu and Kashmir
 and accusing its “so-called” civilian governments of serving “at the mercy” of the army.
Exercising its Right of Reply during a Third Committee meeting, first secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Bhavika Mangalanandan said Pakistan’s civilian governments “rarely complete their terms”, while accusing Islamabad of using cross-border terrorism to divert attention from domestic discontent.
Accoridng to news agency PTI, India “categorically” rejected Pakistan’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were, are and will always remain “integral and inalienable” parts of India.
“We all know that the so-called civilian governments in Pakistan serve at the mercy of their army and rarely complete their terms,” Mangalanandan said.
Referring to jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan, she said a “former Prime Minister continues to remain in jail, even as his health is reported to be fast deteriorating.”
She also said the erstwhile ruling party had not been allowed to contest elections.
“Instead of addressing domestic discontent, Pakistan seeks to distract by fomenting instability in India and sponsoring, inciting, abetting, and financing cross-border terrorism in my country for more than three decades,” she said.
Turning to Jammu and Kashmir, Mangalanandan said, “The only outstanding matter is a vacation of the territory Pakistan holds under illegal and forcible occupation.
She accused Pakistan of attempting to divert attention from unrest in the country.
“This is a desperate attempt by Pakistan to mask the ongoing tragedy in Rawalakot and its other cities, the killing of hundreds of civilians, and the brutal crackdown across Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, for merely demanding bread, electricity and human dignity,” she said.
India also invoked the term “Form 47”, used in reference to allegations of rigging and manipulation in Pakistan’s 2024 general elections.
“When any free media is banned from covering such news in Pakistan, the evidence becomes undeniable for the global community that only the writ of the Form 47 government and their masters and the army headquarters runs large,” she said.
Contrasting this with Jammu and Kashmir, India said Assembly Elections were held there in 2024, followed by a peaceful transfer of power to an elected government.
“The contrast could not have been starker. The only human rights violation taking place in Kashmir is perpetrated by the armed forces of Pakistan and their terrorist proxies. Propaganda does not become fact through repetition,” Mangalanandan said.
“Pakistan would serve its people better by confronting its own fault lines and building its economy than by coveting the territory of others,” she added.

The claim is correct in that Florida became the first state to implement item-specific restrictions for recipients of its Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program at the point of sale. However ...
... other states across the U.S. also block similar purchases through other means. So while the claim is technically correct, Florida is not the first state to block the purchase of certain kinds of items using government funds through other means.
In September 2026, a claim circulated online that Florida had become the first U.S. state to bar recipients of temporary cash assistance from spending it on "nonessential" items such as tattoos, tobacco, drugs, pornography and more.
For example, one popular Facebook post with more than 120,000 likes reads, in part (archived):
The program, funded through the federal TANF [Temporary Assistance for Needy Families] program and delivered via EBT [electronic benefit transfer] cards, gives eligible families with children under 18 an average of about $250 a month for basic living costs. Under the amended plan, that money can no longer go toward tobacco and nicotine products, vaping devices, drugs or intoxicants, p*rnography, video games, theme park admission, entertainment subscriptions, tattoos and body piercings, spa and tanning services, or psychic and fortune-telling services.
(Facebook user It's A Guy Thing)
In short, the claim is correct in that Florida has become the first state to implement item-specific restrictions for TANF recipients at the point of sale, but other states across the U.S. also block similar purchases through other means. So while the claim is technically correct, Florida is not the first state to block the purchase of certain kinds of items using government funds through other means.
Some posts, such as the one above, do not specify the date that the change took place — potentially misleading people into believing the change occurred in September. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis actually first announced the move on Aug. 24, 2026 (archived).
In a news release published that same day, De Santis said (archived):
Florida has become the first in the nation to set guardrails on our TANF State Plan to stop these taxpayer-funded benefits from being used to purchase inappropriate, luxury, and non-essential goods and services. Taxpayer-funded assistance should help families put food on the table, keep the lights on, purchase clothing, provide for their children and overcome barriers on the path toward independence. We will continue supporting Floridians who genuinely need assistance, while working to improve accountability and transparency so that these programs operate as intended.
The full list of new prohibited products was outlined in the 2026-2028 Florida TANF State Plan as follows:
- Tobacco, Nicotine, Vaping and other associated products
- Drugs, intoxicants, and related products
- Pornography, sexually explicit materials, and adult-oriented goods or services
- Entertainment goods, subscriptions, and services such as video games, entertainment tickets, theme parks, and subscriptions/memberships
- Body art, jewelry and body piercings, cosmetic services and luxury items such as tattoos, spa services, and tanning
- Psychic, fortune-telling and divination goods or services
- Political contributions
- Lottery tickets and entries, sports wagers and bets
- Soda
- Energy drinks
- Candy
- Ultra-processed prepared desserts
Further down in De Santis' announcement, it notes that the state already prohibits several kinds of items using welfare assistance:
Florida already prohibits EBT card use or acceptance for alcohol purchases and transactions at adult entertainment establishments, pari-mutuel wagering facilities, slot machine facilities, commercial bingo establishments and casinos or gaming facilities. Florida's EBT vendor blocks point-of-sale transactions at those businesses and ATM transactions at prohibited locations. The first-in-the-nation policy expands those controls to additional items and services at eligible retailers.
The difference between Florida and other states is that it amended its existing limits for purchases at certain locations (such as liquor stores or casinos) to include the use of temporary cash assistance for specific items at the point of sale (PDF page 69).
Some items, including drugs such as recreational marijuana, are already criminalized in the state of Florida.

Pointing out that high-cost medicines used to treat cancer, kidney ailments, and AIDS are being sold at prices up to “70 times higher” than the rates at which dealers and stockists procure them, Karnataka Health Minister U.T. Khader has written a letter to Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda, seeking national action against “abnormal gaps” in drug prices.
The Minister said dealers and stockists purchase advanced pharmaceuticals from manufacturers at heavily discounted wholesale landed rates, while the MRPs printed on the medicines are fixed at “inflated, highly disproportionate levels”. The letter said the gap between the procurement price and MRP was “sometimes 30 times to more than 70 times”.
Mr. Khader said that the issue was particularly concerning for in-patients, emergency and intensive-care patients, oncology patients, and those requiring implants, surgical consumables, and other hospital-based treatment, as they cannot realistically compare suppliers or defer purchases.
The letter said that while the existing MRP framework prevents medicines from being sold above the printed MRP, it does not address situations where the MRP itself has little relation to the actual institutional transaction price, adding that hospitals retain an excessive undisclosed margin.
Mr. Khader sought a national study comparing the printed MRP, manufacturer/importer price, hospital’s net acquisition price, and the price ultimately billed to patients for selected high-value medicines, medical devices, and consumables. He also proposed that the patient-facing price of products supplied through hospitals be capped at the lower end of the applicable statutory price, MRP or the hospital’s net acquisition cost plus a notified and reasonable service margin and applicable taxes.
The Minister said Karnataka would “cooperate with any pilot or national framework” and could, within its powers, make private hospitals disclose more information, require detailed bills for patients, and set up a system to handle complaints locally. However, he said the Centre needs to fix the basic problem — the large difference between what hospitals pay for medicines, the MRP printed on them and what patients are finally charged.

Andhra Pradesh is working to transform itself into a developed State and contribute to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat, says HRD Minister Nara Lokesh.
Speaking at the Pan-IIT Summit 2026 here on Saturday, Mr. Lokesh said the State government’s strategy was centred on “speed, service and stability,” with a focus on converting investment commitments into projects, jobs and long-term economic growth.
He said the government was targeting leadership across key sectors and relying on a combination of experienced leadership and a younger political team. “Nearly half of the MLAs and 17 of the 25 Ministers are first-time legislators and Ministers respectively,” he said.
On governance, Mr. Lokesh said policies should withstand legal scrutiny and political transitions. He said the government was using Artificial Intelligence to analyse previous recruitment orders and court cases while framing new policies. He cited the recruitment of nearly 16,000 teachers as an example of using technology to identify weaknesses in earlier processes and reduce the risk of legal challenges.
The Minister said the State was moving beyond signing MoUs to ensuring their implementation. He cited the proposed Indian School of Agriculture at Madanapalle, which was intended to support an integrated horticulture ecosystem covering research, mechanisation, processing and market access. “The government estimates the ecosystem can attract investments of nearly ₹1 lakh crore,” he said.
Mr. Lokesh also referred to the proposed 17-million-tonne ArcelorMittal greenfield steel project, saying that it progressed from initial discussions with Aditya Mittal to foundation-laying in about 17 months, including environmental clearances.
He said the Google data-centre investment had strengthened Visakhapatnam’s position on the global technology map and credited coordination between the State and Union governments for resolving regulatory and taxation issues.
Growth clusters
He said Andhra Pradesh was also supporting emerging sectors such as space, drones and quantum technology. The government had allotted 300 acres to space startup Skyroot, while waterfront access had been provided to maritime-drone company Sagar Defence.
The State was developing 23 sectoral growth clusters covering areas including horticulture, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, automotive, renewable energy, solar manufacturing, semiconductors, quantum technology, space and defence, he said, adding that Andhra Pradesh added about 4.8 GW of renewable-energy capacity in a year and aimed to move from third position to first.
He stressed the need for both vertical integration of industrial supply chains and horizontal integration linking industry with education, skills, research and testing, and urged the Pan-IIT community to help connect Andhra Pradesh with industry experts and alumni to strengthen the State’s cluster strategy. He also called for collaboration on what he termed “Visible Governance, Invisible Government” by institutionalising faster government processes.
On Amaravati, Mr. Lokesh said the government was developing the capital as a major urban, education and research hub. He also announced plans for a 5,000-acre greenfield airport in Amaravati.

Pakistan-China 5th gen fighter jet plan a concern, but we possess necessary capabilities: IAF Chief
Singh stressed on effectiveness of a fighter aircraft depends not only on the platform itself but also on how well it is integrated.
Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal A P Singh on Saturday said Pakistan's reported collaboration with China on fifth-generation fighter jets is a cause for concern for India, but added that the Indian Air Force has the capabilities to deal with the threat for now.
Speaking at an annual press conference ahead of Air Force Day, Singh said India needs to accelerate the induction of fifth-generation fighter aircraft and push ahead with the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme.
"Reports suggest that Pakistan may acquire them in the near future. There are even reports that their pilots are already undergoing training in China. Undoubtedly, this is a cause for concern. However, is it a no-go situation? I wouldn't agree with that," he said.
Singh stressed that the effectiveness of a fighter aircraft depends not only on the platform itself but also on how well it is integrated with other military capabilities.
“Pakistan has possessed other platforms in the past, yet they haven't been able to achieve anything significant with them during Operation Sindoor. Similarly, if we effectively integrate the platforms we are purchasing and inducting, we should be able to counter this threat—at least for the time being, until they fully integrate these new aircraft into their own systems,” the Air Chief Marshal said.
He further said India cannot afford delays in acquiring aircraft of the next generation and would need to consider alternatives if the AMCA programme does not progress as planned.
"We must prioritise the early induction of an aircraft of this generation. We need to push the AMCA program forward; if there are delays, we must make alternative decisions," he also added.
Also Read | Delay in induction of new fighter jets hurting IAF, says Air Chief
India looks to finalise MRFA deal
India is looking to finalise the much-awaited multi-role fighter aircraft (MRFA) deal within the current financial year, provided the ongoing process proceeds as planned, Singh said.
The government in February cleared a long-pending proposal to procure 114 Rafale fighter jets from France under a government-to-government framework. The proposed acquisition is aimed at strengthening the combat capability of the Indian Air Force.
The deal follows nearly two decades of efforts to expand the IAF's fighter aircraft fleet. Price negotiations and other key issues related to the proposed acquisition are currently underway.
Singh also disclosed that Russia has offered its Su-57 fighter jets to India, although no decision has been taken on the proposal.
"Russia has offered us Su-57 jets, but no decision has been made on it," he said.
Also Read | Watch: India's Tejas, French Rafale, US' F-35 and Russian-made Sukhoi fly together at Tarang Shakti
IAF needs more fighter aircraft
On the declining strength of the IAF's fighter squadrons, Singh said the force needs to induct at least 36 to 40 aircraft every year over the next few years.
He stressed that air power remains an important component of India's overall military capability and said the country needs to continue strengthening its air power.
The Air Chief also spoke about the role of emerging technologies in the IAF's modernisation, particularly artificial intelligence.
"We have to have an AI-augmented force," he said.
Singh further emphasised the importance of self-reliance in strengthening India's combat preparedness.
He also underlined the need for India to develop and manufacture a fighter jet engine domestically as part of its efforts to build indigenous aerospace capabilities.

“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that”, Trivedi said (Photo credit: AP).
NEW DELHI: The Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh on Saturday said Dhaka’s extradition request for ousted ex-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was being legally examined, so New Delhi could not state a deadline for her return.“Nobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasina’s return),” High commissioner Dinesh Trivedi remarked during a discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. PTI reported.“Again and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,” Trivedi added.Hasina sought asylum in India after a massive anti-establishment agitation led to the collapse of her government in August 2024.Trivedi said New Delhi had no role in Hasina’s extraction. She was escorted by a Bangladeshi military detachment from her residence and brought to India through a Bangladeshi aircraft.“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that”, Trivedi said.Trivedi alleged the situation emerged because of “tragic circumstances” in Bangladesh, adding that such circumstances should never be repeated anywhere in the world.
“What was our choice?” Trivedi asked, pointing at the uncertainty of the potential situation, had India denied entry to Hasina’s aircraft.
Strained ties
India-Bangladesh ties severely deteriorated after Hasina sought asylum in Delhi.Hasina was replaced by an interim government led by Mohammad Yunus, which repeatedly called for her extraction from India.During that 18-month interim rule, Hasina was tried in absentia by a special tribunal and sentenced to death; her Awami League party was also disbanded.Following the February 12 elections, Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) came to power. Its government endorsed the ban on Hasina's party and repeatedly renewed the demand for her extradition.However, relations never fully recovered despite a new government in Bangladesh.They were strained further when Hasina addressed a virtual press conference from New Delhi on 5 August 2026, the second anniversary of her removal from power. Bangladesh's foreign ministry had earlier said that the atmosphere for Rahman's visit had been "vitiated" by Hasina's virtual press interaction.India has maintained that it had no role in the media event and that it does not endorse anything said at the forum about the Bangladesh government.
Rahman had declined the invitation to attend the BRICS outreach summit, while a separate bilateral invitation has been on hold since February.Despite the downturn in bilateral relations, Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, said after meeting Trivedi on Tuesday that Dhaka was "positive" about progress in discussions on Rahman's proposed visit to India; PTI reported that no date has been fixed yet.

Tennessee’s top prison official is stepping down in the aftermath of the failed execution of death row prisoner Christa Pike, the state’s governor Bill Lee announced Saturday.
Frank Strada, the department of correction commissioner, will leave his position later in October as the state launches an independent investigation into what went wrong during Wednesday’s botched execution of Pike, according to Lee.
Strada for his part said his resignation would allow that review to move forward in the best interests of Tennessee.
“Serving as commissioner of the Tennessee department of correction has been a great honor, and I continue to believe the department carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol,” Strada said in his resignation statement.
“Even so, stepping aside is in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward,” he said. “I believe this review is entirely appropriate and necessary, and I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred.”
Strada handed in his resignation amid intensifying scrutiny of Tennessee’s closely guarded execution procedures after Pike was injected with lethal drugs on Wednesday but survived. She became the first death row prisoner in the US to undergo such an execution attempt and live.
Pike’s attorney Randy Spivey, who witnessed the procedure from inside the death chamber, described what happened as “cruel and torturous”. He said he personally counted seven needles inserted into Pike’s left arm, “one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her”.
Attorneys have alleged that Pike’s failed lethal injection was the fifth “botched” execution carried out under Strada’s leadership in two states since 2022, as the Guardian reported on Saturday, hours before his resignation was announced.
Pike remained unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital as of Friday, according to a court filing submitted by her attorneys. Her lawyers said hospital personnel were trying to save her life and, as of late Thursday, were working to clear the two doses of the execution drug from her system.
Wednesday’s extraordinary breakdown inside Tennessee’s execution chamber has triggered demands for an explanation from people on both sides of the death penalty debate. Besides ordering the independent review into case, Lee has paused the scheduling of executions in Tennessee.
Pike’s attorneys said they believe complications involving intravenous lines caused pentobarbital to enter her body rather than her bloodstream.
“Frank Strada’s resignation does not change the fact that Tennessee is shrouding its executions in secrecy,” Kit Thomas, a death row attorney in the federal public defender’s office in Nashville, said in a statement. “When Governor Lee hired Strada to fix execution problems in Tennessee his problematic history of executions in Arizona was well known. Strada then oversaw the implementation of a new protocol that ignored the recommendations of the independent investigation and weakened protections leading to a string of problems in Tennessee, including this week’s horrific botched execution attempt and another one in May. Until there is transparency and accountability, botched executions will keep happening.”
Pike, 50, was sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of teenage classmate Colleen Slemmer. Pike and her then boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, killed Slemmer at a job training camp in Knoxville.
A pentagram had been carved into Slemmer’s chest.
After the murder, Pike was diagnosed with bipolar and post-traumatic stress disorders, her attorneys said.
“It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done,” Pike had said in an earlier petition for clemency. “Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone’s child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime.”
Had her execution that day succeeded, Pike on Wednesday would have been the first woman put to death in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

Devendra Fadnavis pushes for use of Marathi in AI, space tech and biotechnology
Devendra Fadnavis said Maharashtra will expand Marathi use in AI, quantum computing, space technology and biotechnology. The push aims to preserve the language's heritage while making it central to modern knowledge and digital life.
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday said efforts would be made to strengthen Marathi as a digital and knowledge language in the 21st century by increasing its use in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, quantum computing, space technology and biotechnology.
Speaking at the inauguration of the 'Classical Marathi Language Week' and 'Classical Marathi Language Honour Day' programme at SNDT Women's University in Mumbai, Fadnavis said Marathi must be used more widely in everyday life as well as in modern technology. Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and Marathi Language and Industries Minister Uday Samant also outlined steps being taken to promote the language in India and abroad.
Fadnavis said, "Marathi is not merely a medium of communication but a carrier of our rich culture and a witness to our glorious history." He said Marathi's rich vocabulary, literary tradition and diverse dialects were important parts of its heritage and should be preserved while making the language relevant to new areas of knowledge.
"Marathi should be used more extensively in artificial intelligence and digital technology. Knowledge related to quantum computing, space technology and biotechnology should also be made available in Marathi," he said. He also called for greater availability of Marathi information and knowledge content on digital platforms, OTT services and social media, and said the Centre's recognition of Marathi as a classical language was a matter of pride for Marathi speakers.
Referring to the Marathi encyclopaedia and dictionaries, Fadnavis said the language had a rich vocabulary and stressed the need to expand the words recorded in government-published Marathi dictionaries through successive editions. He also underlined the need to preserve dialects such as Konkani, Varhadi, Khandeshi-Ahirani, Malvani, Dangi and Zhadiboli, saying they reflected local culture, traditions and experiences. "Marathi's preservation and promotion should not remain limited to government initiatives. People must increase its use at home, in education, administration, business, technology and social media," he said.
Shinde said Marathi was not only Maharashtra's identity but also its pride, and added that the language had spread beyond the state's borders. "The next World Marathi Literary Conference will be held in London. A 'Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Global Marathi Centre' is also being planned there. Around 70,000 to 80,000 Marathi-speaking people live in London," he said. He also urged people to gift Marathi books instead of bouquets on occasions such as birthdays and felicitation ceremonies to encourage reading.
Samant said the state government was working on a Centre of Excellence for Marathi at Deccan College in Pune, a global Marathi centre in London, dictionaries covering 100 dialects and Marathi skill development centres at nine locations. He said the number of international Marathi forums had reached 52 and the government aimed to increase it to 75.
Marathi Language Department Secretary Kiran Kulkarni said the language's tradition could be traced back to the Gatha Saptashati, dating back around 2,500 years. He said the department was focusing on research, preservation and digitisation of Marathi's classical heritage, with special emphasis on involving young people. Kulkarni said the Marathi encyclopaedia, whose creation began under the guidance of Tarkateerth Laxmanshastri Joshi, was being digitised and would be fully available on a portal from this month. The programme also saw the release of the book Marathiche Kautuk Part-2 and a cultural programme on the theme 'Classical Marathi, Pride Marathi', bringing together the main efforts announced for the language's promotion and preservation.

The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Republic of Korea have a long-standing partnership spanning over 75 years. As a result of their fruitful collaboration, there has been significant progress in health and development all around the world. The Republic of Korea has gone from being a donor-recipient country to a donor-country and is now a leader in global health and playing a critical role on the world stage.
Dr Catharina Boehme, Assistant Director-General for External Relations and Governance (WHO) and Dr Hye-Jin Kim, Deputy Minister for Planning and Coordination (Ministry of Health and Welfare, Republic of Korea), together with counterparts from WHO and the Government of the Republic of Korea. © WHO
To further strengthen this partnership and our commitment to working jointly to address global health challenges, WHO and the Republic of Korea convened their second Strategic Dialogue in Seoul from 28 to 29 August 2024. Dr Catharina Boehme, Assistant Directory-General for External Relations and Governance, led the WHO delegation and was accompanied by an in-person team and colleagues participating virtually from the three levels of the Organization (headquarters, regional, and country offices).
Dr Hye-Jin Kim, Deputy Minister for Planning and Coordination, Ministry of Health, led the Republic of Korea delegation and was joined by senior officials including Dr Young-Mee Jee, Commissioner, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, as well as senior counterparts from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
In addition, in line with WHO's work to enhance collaboration with parliamentarians, the WHO delegation also met with various Members of the National Assembly that are championing the global health agenda.
The recently concluded two-day meeting resulted in an alignment of priorities and paved the way for enhanced collaboration between WHO and the Government of Korea.

Chief Minister Omar Abdullah today witnessed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Jammu & Kashmir Bank Ltd and Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS), aimed at expanding healthcare access and strengthening institutional financial services across Jammu and Kashmir.
The MoU was signed by Director SKIMS Prof. Mohammad Ashraf Ganie on behalf of SKIMS and J&K Bank MD & CEO Amitava Chatterjee on behalf of J&K Bank Ltd.
Minister for Health & Medical Education Sakina Itoo, Advisor to the Chief Minister Nasir Aslam Wani among others, were present on the occasion.
The agreement brings together the J&K’s premier tertiary-care institution and its leading financial institution to facilitate patient services, employee welfare, financial inclusion and support for healthcare infrastructure.
A key feature of the MoU is the integration of SKIMS’ OPD ticketing and appointment booking system with the Banking Correspondent (BC) network of J&K Bank on a six-month pilot basis. The initiative will enable patients in far-flung and rural areas to obtain SKIMS OPD tickets and appointments locally, reducing the need for them to travel to Srinagar solely for the purpose of booking appointments.
Under the agreement, SKIMS has nominated J&K Bank as a banking partner and extended customized benefits to its regular employees, including zero-balance salary accounts, waiver of specified banking charges, concessional loan rates, auto-sweep facilities among other facilities.
The MoU also provides for dedicated counters at SKIMS for J&K Bank employees, while SKIMS will depute a physician to the Bank’s headquarters once every month to facilitate medical consultations for its staff.
The partnership also envisages greater institutional support for patients and healthcare infrastructure. J&K Bank will prioritize CSR assistance for SKIMS hospital infrastructure and integrate the SKIMS Endowment Fund for poor patients with its Mpay Delight+ mobile application, enabling members of the public to contribute directly towards patient support.
As part of the agreement, J&K Bank will also conduct fully funded digital financial literacy camps for SKIMS personnel and organize quarterly sessions on wealth management.

Protesters across Spain demand action over housing crisis
- Published
Thousands of protesters have taken to the streets across Spain calling for greater protections for tenants after the government failed to get emergency housing legislation through parliament on Friday.
About 50 planned marches were expected to take place in cities such as Madrid, Valencia and Barcelona on Saturday - with some already under way.
"There is a lot of anger in the streets," said a spokesperson for the Valencia Tenants' Union, where a demonstration has already started. Clashes have taken place between some protesters and police in the city.
The measures put forward by Pedro Sánchez's leftist coalition government on Friday followed public outcry over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home last month after she was unable to afford a sharp rent increase.
Her eviction triggered nationwide protests across Spain with protesters demanding lower rents, an end to evictions, and a ban on investment funds - or "vulture funds" as the government has termed them - buying property.
Sanchez's defeat in Congress on Friday heightens speculation that he might call an early general election, which was not due until next summer.
His coalition government, made up of his ruling Socialist party and junior partner the Sumar alliance, does not command a majority in parliament.

Photographs showed protesters in the east coast city of Valencia clashing with police officers on Saturday near arts centre Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía, which was hosting a real estate summit.
Several protesters removed barriers and threw objects at officers, who responded with rubber bullets, Spanish media reported.
The biggest demonstration was expected to take place in the capital Madrid. Demonstrators have been camping in one of the city's main squares, Puerta del Sol, for days.
One protester, David, told Spanish public broadcaster RTVE ahead of the protest: "We're not here for pleasure or comfort. We're here out of conviction."
On Friday night, the Madrid's Tenants' Union said that although the government's proposed measures were insufficient, the rejection of the proposed legislation "exacerbates the housing crisis which is costing the working class their lives".
It is calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.
The legislation put forward in Congress on Friday was divided into two separate decrees.
The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by so-called "vulture funds".
The second decree included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Tenant's Union.
MPs rejected the first decree by 178 votes to 172 and voted against the second by 184 to 166.
Prior to the vote, the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.
However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.
Sánchez's ruling coalition hurriedly drew up the decree laws in an effort to defuse the housing protests that were sparked when 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted in September.
The social backlash led to the company that owns Abascal's flat, Urbagestión, negotiating her return to the flat on a low rent. However, protests have continued.

On August 1, 2026, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari claimed that of the 27 lakh people whose names were deleted from the voter list after adjudication due to ‘logical discrepancy’, only seven lakh had filed appeals before the court-appointed appellate tribunals seeking inclusion in the electoral rolls.
Speaking at the launch of the Census self-enumeration exercise in Kolkata, he said, “Out of the 27 lakh people who were given an opportunity to approach the SIR tribunal, around seven lakh had applied. The rest have not submitted any application or appeal so far.”
The figure was reported by multiple media outlets which quoted the chief minister (1, 2, 3). Adhikari went on to link the failure to appeal with questions of citizenship, and citizenship with access to welfare, saying, “Until the entire process was completed, it would not be possible to determine whether those who had not made any claim as voters would later seek recognition as Indian citizens.” He added, “If someone is not a citizen of the country, they will not get benefits of any social scheme.”
Five days later, The Telegraph published the same seven-lakh figure, this time attributing it to an unnamed senior official of the West Bengal government. According to the report, the official said, “It has been found that only about 7 lakh of the 27 lakh voters excluded by the adjudicators for ‘logical discrepancies’ have appealed before the tribunals.” The official said the figure had emerged from a compilation of reports from various districts, and that the state authorities had no idea why the remaining 20 lakh had not appealed before the tribunals.
The Figure was Unverifiable at that Time
In August, the seven-lakh claim could not be independently verified against any official source because the Election Commission’s own disclosure did not provide a separate breakdown of appeals filed against the exclusion of voters. An RTI reply that disclosed the total number of appeals carried a footnote clarifying that the figure included both appeals against the inclusion of names in the electoral roll and appeals against exclusions.
The RTI was obtained by Isha Khan Choudhury, Congress MP from Dakshin Malda in West Bengal, and placed before the Supreme Court on August 24, 2026, during the hearing of a petition filed by Prasenjit Bose of the Congress and Derek O’Brien of the Trinamool Congress against the Election Commission of India.
During the hearing, Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that the break-up of the appeals mattered since “it was exclusion which was causing an immediate violation of a person’s rights.” The bench consequently directed the ECI to provide a separate account of the appeals, specifying how many were pending before the tribunals and segregating appeals relating to voters who had been excluded or included, as well as cross-appeals.
The ECI submitted this segregation on September 16.
ECI Numbers Refute Adhikari’s Claim
According to the latest affidavit filed by the ECI before the Supreme Court on September 16, 2026, of the more than 38.31 lakh appeals filed, over 22 lakh were filed against exclusion by voters whose names had been excluded or deleted, while more than 16 lakh were filed against inclusion.
Of the more than 38 lakh appeals filed, only 1.26 lakh had been decided by that date. Annexure R/1 to the ECI’s affidavit provides a district-wise break-up of the total appeals submitted to the appellate tribunals and is reproduced below.
It must be noted that the total number of appeals filed, as mentioned in the ECI’s affidavit (38,31,429), does not match the total number of appeals submitted in Annexure R/1 (38,29,926). The discrepancy is 1,503 appeals. Nevertheless, the outcome-wise data provided in the annexure shows that 8,649 appeals resulted in exclusion from the electoral roll, while 1,13,943 resulted in inclusion. In other words, nearly 93% of the appeals that had been decided resulted in the elector being included in the electoral roll.
Did the Claims Accumulate after the CM’s Statement? No
One may argue that the chief minister spoke on August 1, while the Commission filed its figure in the Supreme Court on September 16, leaving enough time for appeals to have accumulated in the intervening period. The available data, however, allows this possibility to be tested directly, because appeal totals are available for both dates. On August 7, 2026, six days after the chief minister’s statement and a day after The Telegraph report, the tribunals already had 38,10,620 appeals, according to an RTI response from the ECI to Isha Khan Choudhury, Congress MP for Dakshin Malda. By September 10, 2026, the figure stood at 38,29,926, according to the district-wise report annexed to the Commission’s affidavit. Thus, the total number of appeals increased by just 19,306 across the entire state during this period.
In the light of the latest revelations made by an Indian Express investigation, which have raised serious questions about the functioning of the Election Commission of India and chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the seven-lakh claim takes on an even greater significance.
To sum up, Suvendu Adhikari’s claim on August 1 that out of some 27 lakh electors placed under adjudication and subsequently excluded from the electoral roll, only seven lakh had appealed against their exclusion is difficult to reconcile with the data that was already available at the time. The ECI has made it clear that the number is around 22 lakh. The discrepancy assumes greater significance given that Manoj Agarwal, the then chief electoral officer of West Bengal who oversaw the SIR process, is now the Bengal’s chief secretary.

Volodymyr Zelensky has said Russian president Vladimir Putin has instructed his generals to abandon the rules of war to capture more territory in Ukraine.
Russia has increasingly targeted Ukrainian cities, hitting key infrastructure that is keeping Ukraine’s war-battered economy afloat.
Recent targets have included key industries, railways, data centres, energy infrastructure, as well as schools and hospitals.
"He said there are no rules now,” the Ukrainian president said yesterday, citing intelligence from intercepted communications from Kremlin officials, the Financial Times reported.
Russian attacks on a key bridge over the Dnipro River over consecutive days have forced traffic chaos across it.
A drone struck the Souther Bridge at 5.40pm local time yesterday, coinciding with the Ukrainian capital city’s evening rush hour.
The attack led to long traffic jams across the city throughout the day.
Zelensky says Putin has told his generals 'there are no rules now' in Ukraine war
Volodymyr Zelensky says Russian president Vladimir Putin has instructed his generals to abandon the rules of war in pursuit of more territory in Ukraine, according to the Financial Times.
The Ukrainian president made the remarks during a visit to a bomb shelter inside a school that had been hit by a Russian drone on Thursday.
Zelensky said Putin gave the order last month, saying: "He said there are no rules now." Russia has since stepped up its air strikes on civilian targets, particularly in Kyiv, hitting data centres and energy infrastructure as well as schools and hospitals.
Russia still formally denies that it strikes civilian targets, and typically justifies its strikes as hitting military-linked buildings or infrastructure.
Zelensky cited intelligence from intercepted communications from Kremlin officials, the FT reported.
Russian strikes on Kyiv bridge causes traffic chaos
Russia struck a bridge over the Dnipro River that linked two sides of Kyiv, forcing full or partial traffic suspension across it.
A drone struck the Souther Bridge around 5.40pm local time yesterday, marking the second attack on the structure in two days.
Nearly 90 per cent of transit traffic between the two banks of the river passes through the Southern Bridge.
The latest attack also coincided with Kyiv's evening rush hour.
The Russian aerial attacks on the bridge are part of an intensifying campaign on infrastructure across Kyiv, disrupting daily life in the Ukrainian capital.
They have led to long traffic jams across the city throughout the day.
North Korea test-fires missile as tensions grow over border mine blasts
North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile toward the sea on Saturday, South Korea’s military said, extending a recent run of weapons tests during heightened tensions between the rivals over border land mine blasts that injured three South Korean soldiers.
South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the missile being launched from the North’s eastern coastal Wonsan area, but didn’t immediately say how far the weapon flew. Japanese broadcaster NHK reported that the missile likely landed outside the country’s exclusive economic zone.
The South’s joint chiefs said the military stepped up surveillance and vigilance for possible further launches from the North and was closely sharing information with the United States and Japan.

Four injured in Russian attacks on pharmaceutical warehouse in Kyiv oblast
At least four people are injured following Russian drone strikes at warehouses in Kyiv Oblast today.
The injured include an 8-year-old child, who suffered a shrapnel wound to the lower limb, according to Kyiv Oblast Military Administration head Tymur Tkachenko.
One of the targeted sites was a warehouse of Ukraine's third-largest pharmaceutical distributor, Venta LTD.
First US critical minerals deal with Ukraine unveiled
The joint US–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF) unveiled America's first-ever critical minerals deal with Ukrainian company BGV Group Management, valued at around $30 million.
It comes after Kyiv signed the so-called "minerals deal" with the US in April last year, establishing a joint investment fund in Ukraine that gives the US favourable access to mineral-related investment projects in Ukraine.
The project will see URIF develop a "joint investment platform" with the BGV Group, founded by Ukrainian billionaire Hennadii Butkevych.
It will "build a diverse portfolio of early-stage mining projects across Ukraine" with a focus on identifying rare earths, beryllium, and zirconium deposits, according to URIF.
Embassies 'not planning evacuation' in Kyiv amid Russian strikes, Ukrainian foreign ministry says
Ukraine's presidential office said it has not received notifications from any foreign embassy in Kyiv regarding an intent to evacuate the Ukrainian capital city.
"If any diplomatic missions are planning to relocate, they inform us; that is the established procedure," Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi said today, adding that no such requests have been made.
His comments came after The Guardian reported, citing an unnamed diplomat, that the situation in Kyiv was "obviously deteriorating fast", and embassies could be planning to evacuate.
"As of now, the Foreign Ministry has not received any such requests or notifications from foreign diplomatic missions regarding plans to relocate," Tykhyi said.
EU says situation in Russian-occupied Oleshky is appalling
Russia must provide humanitarian assistance to civilians in the Ukrainian town of Oleshky — currently occupied by Russia — as the situation there is "appalling", European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib, whose portfolio includes humanitarian aid, said on Friday.
"What is happening in Oleshky, Ukraine, is appalling. Civilians are trapped under siege by Russian forces without access to food, medicine, clean water and basic care. This is unacceptable," said Lahbib.
"Russia, as occupying power, has clear obligations under international humanitarian law: civilians must be protected and humanitarian assistance must be facilitated," she added.

Former German chancellor with links to Putin joins board of Russian retailer
Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder, who has faced criticism over his links to Russian business and President Vladimir Putin, has joined the supervisory board of Russian retailer Hyperglobus, the company said on Friday.
Schroeder formed a close relationship with Putin while serving as German chancellor from 1998 to 2005 and later working for Russian state companies.
Hyperglobus was spun off from Germany's Globus Holding in 2025 and is now fully independent, according to Globus. It operates more than 20 Russian supermarkets that continue to use the Globus brand.
The announcement of Schroeder's appointment came four days after Putin issued a decree placing the Russian assets of another big German retailer, Metro, under temporary administration – the latest in a series of moves against businesses from countries that have supported Ukraine against Russia in the war.

Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.
Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.
His full trial has been repeatedly deferred by the authorities in the federal court but largely similar conspiracy charges were dismissed by a court in Punjab last year. Throughout his detention the prosecution has failed to produce verifiable evidence, leading to the deferred hearings.
Johal, now 39, travelled to India to marry his fiancee in late 2017. On 4 November, three weeks after the wedding, the couple were shopping with a relative in the Punjab city of Jalandhar when a group of men took Johal from his car, placed a black hood over his head and put him in an unmarked vehicle. He claims he was then denied access to a lawyer and tortured in an attempt to extract a confession. A question remains over whether he was arrested following a tip-off from British intelligence services.
Commenting on Friday’s ruling, Johal’s Scotland-based brother Gurpreet Singh Johal said: “The past two years has been an expensive rollercoaster, contesting bails at the supreme court and back to the high court. I had a long, sleepless night knowing that the decision would be made this morning. Now, all I can think about is Jagtar walking out of prison. We have waited so long and fought so hard for this moment.”
He added of previous hearings: “Whenever the evidence against Jagtar is tested in court, judges find what we’ve said all along, which is that there isn’t any.
“How long will this sick joke of a legal process be allowed to continue? We’re obviously delighted that Jagtar will soon be released, but he won’t be truly free until he is back in Dumbarton, with his wife and family.”
Gurpreet Johal, who also lives in Dumbarton, has lobbied a succession of UK foreign secretaries, who have repeatedly admitted the case has dragged on too long, but have been reluctant to call publicly for his release on the grounds that they should not interfere in the judiciary of another country.
The UK government recently appointed Alistair Burt as a special envoy for complex consular cases and he has met Gurpreet Johal in Scotland to discuss the case.
Dan Dolan, the deputy executive director of Reprieve, one of the organisation’s fighting for Johal’s release, said: “While this judgment is welcome as Jagtar should not be in prison a day longer, we must now watch closely to ensure this order is actually implemented and not obstructed in any way. The conditions attached are likely to be onerous. We must also remember that Jagtar will still be facing the death penalty in eight cases against him, despite these cases essentially duplicating trumped-up charges on which he has already been fully acquitted.”
Chris Esdaile, a senior legal adviser to Redress, another organisaiton representing Johal, said granting bail “can’t undo the intolerable suffering caused by nine years of arbitrary detention”.
He added: “The need for accountability for the allegations of torture and the deeply flawed proceedings against Jagtar remains urgent.”
Johal’s lawyers said they were still awaiting the details of what would happen next in relation to posting bail terms. While the judges’ order was that Jagtar should be released on bail, he remained in custody while judges confirmed his bail conditions, which may be stringent. The court must also confirm the sums of money that must be posted as a bond.

Legendary cinema director and writer Singeetham Srinivasa Rao passed away on Saturday evening in Chennai in Kauvery Hospital, according to family and friends. He was 94.
Born in Gudur in Nellore district, he burst onto the screen at the age of 41 with his writing and direction of Neeti Nijayati, a Telugu movie with a homily in its heart in 1972. But before that, Singeetham began as a dialogue writer to filmmaker K.V. Reddy and assisted him in the ground breaking Telugu movie in 1957: Mayabazar. Between these two dates, he honed and experimented his craft.
From then onwards, he directed movies in multiple languages including Pushpak Vimana without any dialogue starring Kamal Hassan an Amala. Among the notable movies he helmed or had a role in bringing to screen were: Pantulamma, Zamindaru Gari Ammayi, America Ammayi, Pilla Zamindar, Mayuri, Apoorva Sagodharargal, Michael Madana Kama Rajan, Aditya 369 and dozens of other movies.
Singeetham Srinivasa Rao acted in some movies and even composed the movie score. His last movie was the Sing Geetham, musical-fantasy comedy which he directed and wrote the script. The genre defying movie was released in June 2026 with the director sometimes remotely wielding the mike.

Qatar and Abu Dhabi F1 Grand Prix to go ahead: F1 boss
SEPANG, Malaysia: The final races of the Formula One season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as planned despite tensions in the Middle East, the sport's CEO Stefano Domenicali said Saturday (Oct 3).
"Based on the information we have, everything is confirmed for (us to stay in) Qatar and Abu Dhabi," Domenicali told French broadcaster Canal Plus on the sidelines of the Bahrain Grand Prix, which was relocated to the Sepang circuit in Malaysia this weekend.
Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the boss of motorsport's premier series "confirmed the schedule for the final two Grands Prix" of the year in Qatar on Nov 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec 6.
The Bahrain and Saudi Arabia grands prix were scrapped earlier this season due to the start of the US-led war with Iran.
Italian Domenicali insisted "that everything was in order" and that "teams and drivers were being kept informed of the situation."
He added that 99 percent of tickets had been sold in Abu Dhabi and that the season-ending race was generating "great excitement".
However not all drivers want to compete in the Gulf.
Dutch four-time world champion Max Verstappen, who will start from pole position in Malaysia on Sunday, said during the week he would prefer if the season did not finish in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
"Normally I am happy to go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi, but you know, when there is a war nearby, and if some of the countries are in conflict with each other, then I think we shouldn't go," he told ViaPlay.
"Then, it doesn't matter if you have a contract or not, I think. But it's not up to me."
One of the Plan B options discussed was moving the Emirati race to Imola in Italy.

The government has revised the FASTag rules for vehicles registered under the 'Divyangjan' category and persons with disabilities (PwD). As per the new rules, these vehicles will get an exempted FASTag based on the percentage of disability recorded in a valid disability certificate, unique disability identity (UDID) card or other applicable records
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) said it has revised the guidelines to promote ease of living for the citizens and further simplify toll-related procedures for eligible beneficiaries.
What has changed for the eligible beneficiaries?
Earlier, guidelines mandated annual renewal of the FASTag exemption for Divyangjan. But now the validity will be decided on the recorded percentage of disability.
"FASTag issued to persons with 70 per cent to 100 per cent disability will be valid for five years, while those issued to persons with 40 per cent to less than 70 per cent disability will be valid for three years," the ministry said.
Also Read | Over one crore FASTag annual passes issued since August 2025 launch: govt
But does this mean eligible Divyangjan will not have to pay tolls for three or five years?
No. The longer validity of the exempted FASTag does not mean that a person is being granted a blanket five-year or three-year waiver from all toll payments. It means the exempted FASTag does not have to be renewed annually during its validity period, subject to the applicable eligibility conditions and toll-exemption rules.
The ministry said the exemption is based on the percentage of disability recorded in a valid disability certificate, Unique Disability Identity (UDID) card or other applicable records.
“Validity of the exempted FASTag will be determined by the recorded percentage of disability,” the ministry said.
The FASTag can be renewed after three or five years, depending on the category, “subject to continued eligibility” and compliance with the National Highways Fee Rules, 2008.
FASTag annual pass reaches one crore milestone
The total number of 'FASTag Annual Pass' has crossed the significant milestone of one crore since its launch on August 15 last year, reflecting strong adoption among National Highway users, an official statement said on 28 September.
The milestone reflects growing acceptance of the Annual Pass among private vehicle owners for providing a seamless and economical travel option on national highways and expressways, it added.
Also Read | NHAI launches OneTag on Rajmargyatra app — How FASTag users benefit
Applicable on about 1,150 fee plazas on national highways and national expressways, the Annual Pass eliminates the need to frequently recharge FASTag through a one-time fee payment of  ₹3,075 for one year validity or 200 toll plaza crossings.
The pass is applicable for all non-commercial vehicles with a valid FASTag. The annual pass gets activated on the existing FASTag linked to the vehicle after a one-time fee payment through the Rajmargyatra app.

Jakarta – Two new islands have emerged in waters surrounding Mount Anak Krakatau following a major eruption last month that grounded flights for days, the head of Indonesia’s volcano monitoring agency said Friday.
The islands were spotted in satellite images of the water-filled caldera in which Anak Krakatau stands, Rita Susilawati of the PVMBG Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said.
“Based on an evaluation of Sentinel satellite imagery, two formations resembling small islands can be seen around Mount Anak Krakatau” in the Sunda Strait between the islands of Java and Sumatra, she added.
Sentinel is a fleet of Earth observation spacecraft developed by the European Space Agency.
One of the islands was located about 760 meters northwest of Mount Anak Krakatau, the other about 495 meters southwest.
Rita said it was too early to refer to the islands as “children” of Mount Anak Krakatau — which itself was formed by an underwater eruption in the caldera or depression left behind after the massive 1883 blowout of the original Krakatau volcano.
“Anak” means child in Bahasa Indonesia.
Rita said further research was needed to determine if the new islands were emerging from the base of the caldera in a similar way than Anak Krakatau did, or whether they were formed by deposits of volcanic material.
In the case of Anak Krakatau, several landmasses briefly emerged starting in 1927 and then disappeared due to erosion before an enduring island formed in 1930, she added.
The two new islands may similarly be eroded away over time.
Mount Anak Krakatau erupted for 25 hours nonstop in September, blanketing cities in volcanic ash and prompting multiple airports to close.
More than 300,000 passengers were left stranded.
Rita said Anak Krakatau was at alert Level 2, the second lowest out of four danger categories.
People are advised not to approach within 3 km of the eruption center.
Five journalists on a mission to cover the September eruption were declared presumed dead, along with three boat crewmembers, nearly two weeks after the vessel they were traveling in disappeared without a trace.
Indonesia sits on the Ring of Fire, where the meeting of continental plates causes high volcanic and seismic activity.
