A smart cat tracker is like a wearable health-monitoring device, such as a smart ring, smartwatch, or fitness tracker, that helps people stay on top of key wellness markers—but for a cat.
Why should humans have all the fun? In addition to live and historical GPS location tracking that helps any helicopter cat parent rest easy, the Fi Mini, Tractive Smart Cat Tracker, and Tractive Cat 6 Mini monitor your furry friend's health metrics, like activity and sleep. The collars also send alerts for changes in health patterns, such as when your pet is moving less or sleeping more than average, which can serve as early warning signs of potential health issues.
For the better part of the year, I've been testing these trackers on my cat Basil, analyzing each device's location accuracy, sleep- and activity-tracking capabilities, and health summary metrics. I also considered practical factors, such as ease of use, product size, and battery life.
If you have a cat that also goes outdoors, these trackers are much more reliable and comprehensive than something like an AirTag because they determine positioning via satellite instead of the nearest Bluetooth signal. They'll also notify you if your cat leaves your designated “safe zone.”
Ultimately, each smart tracker has its own strengths. The best model for you and your cat depends on your priorities—if you value long battery life, the Fi Mini ($99) is the best choice. If you want advanced health features, the Tractive Cat 6 Mini ($77) is the best smart collar option.
Be sure to check out our related pet guides, like the Best Automatic Litter Boxes, Best Cat Water Fountains, Best Automatic Feeders, and Best Pet Cameras.
In This Guide
Best Connected App
If tracking your cat's location is your top priority, Tractive (also called the Tractive Cat Mini) is the best option. Its historical heat maps show the areas your cat frequents, which is especially helpful for people with indoor–outdoor cats who roam large swaths of land.
However, note that all tested models rely on GPS for location tracking. This means that if the satellite signal is spotty—a common issue in rural areas and other settings—you may not know your cat's precise location. Some Reddit and Amazon reviewers complain that Tractive's location tracking is less accurate in areas with dense vegetation.
In setting up each tracker's connected app, you can designate specific mapped areas as safe or danger zones, and the app will notify you when the pet enters or exits these zones. Basil is an indoor cat, but with all three trackers, my apartment was too small to create a virtual fence around the perimeter, so I had to expand it to an area outside my apartment. That means if Basil got out but stayed nearby, I wouldn't get an alert.
In the Tractive app, after you create a profile, you'll get personalized daily activity goals for your cat based on statistics from other cats of similar age and weight. The app assigned Basil 120 to 230 minutes of daily activity and later reported that he was consistently more active than 70 percent of similar cats. I felt at peace knowing I'm keeping him on the move in my small apartment.
At the end of each day and week, the app provides activity averages and daily calorie estimates, calculated using factors like pet type, weight, and size, and compared with activity output.
Tractive's sleep-tracking feature monitors sleep duration, breaking it down into categories of night sleep, day sleep, and calm. Because it tracks sleep length and cycle phases based on movement patterns and time of day, the data is more general than precise. In general, I found the information in Tractive's app more useful and easier to analyze than in Fi.
Best Battery Life, Charging, and Size
Testing these trackers made me realize the importance of basic features like battery life and ease of removing the tracker from the collar for charging. This is where the Fi Mini shines. (Read my full review here.)
Fi Mini takes about two hours to reach a full charge, which lasted about two weeks in my testing. Fi claims four weeks, but two weeks is much longer than the Tractive, which conked out at around five days on a full charge. While I didn't test this, Fi claims its tracker can hold a six- to eight-week charge with the Fi Base add-on.
In addition to extending battery life by functioning as a connection source when your pet is at home, the Base also supposedly helps with location accuracy thanks to its Wi-Fi connection. One bonus for Fi users with an Apple Watch: You can add the Fi app to your watch to monitor your pet’s location and activity and enter “Lost Mode” without a phone, which is especially helpful if your cat has escaped while you're away from your phone.
The Fi's danger zone alerts were glitchy during my testing. On three occasions, I got notifications that Basil had left the safe zone (aka, my home and surrounding area). Each time, after I rushed home or raced to check my pet camera, I found him sleeping soundly on the living room couch. Other users have reported similar false alerts and location inaccuracy with the Fi.
Charging the Fi was a breeze. It uses the same USB-C charger as my iPhone, making the power-up process convenient and easy. The Tractive not only requires its own dedicated charger but also proved difficult to attach and detach from the device.
On the size front, the Fi Mini tracker is lightweight, small, and compact at just 1.5 x 1.0 x 0.5 inches. It comes with a strap loop and two types of soft cases. I liked the loop attachment best because its stretchy rubber material let me slip the tracker out without fully removing Basil's collar. Both the Tractive device itself and its collar attachment were much bulkier, and I worried they impeded Basil's ability to fully move his head downward.
The Fi Mini offers similar health metrics to the Tractive, but it only compares your pet's statistics against itself (as opposed to similar pets, like the Tractive). I liked that the Fi allows you to add vet records, receipts, and insurance information, and you can add vets to share pet-related documents and get appointment reminders.
Best Health Tracking Features
The Cat 6 Mini is the newest smart collar from Tractive (released earlier this year), now with advanced health features for respiratory and heart rate monitoring, as well as AI-powered weekly health summaries. I compared this new smart collar with the other smart collars I've tested, and although the short battery life is a pain, I recommend this model if measuring your cat's health metrics is your top priority. (Read my review here.)
Unlike the other models that use an attachment that fits on the cat's existing collar, the Tractive Cat 6 Mini device is the entire collar itself, and to charge, you need to remove the collar from the cat. As someone with reduced grip strength, the clasp made this task difficult for me. Like its predecessor, it also uses a proprietary charger. Charging took almost three hours, and it needed to be charged about every four days.
Like the previous model, you create a virtual fence so you'll be alerted if the pet leaves the safe area. Tractive also compares Basil to cats of similar age and weight to set a personalized daily activity goal. With the new Cat 6 Mini model, you'll get an AI summary of the previous week's activity and health stats, along with daily stats and weekly averages for sleep, activity, respiratory rate, and heart rate. Basil's respiratory rate was on the lower end, and his resting heart rate was consistently lower than that of cats of similar age and weight. The app even gave potential reasons and supplemental information for the low heart rate, including “fitness and conditioning” and “cold temperatures.” I'm planning to bring these stats and potential concerns to his next vet appointment.

Also Tested
Moggie Activity Tracker + Hub for $149: The device not only provides metrics on your cat's health but also offers in-depth activity graphs with comparative baselines so you can see what's normal. I liked that it lasted a long time on a charge and was lightweight, small, and easy to take on and off without removing the entire collar. I live in a small apartment with limited outlets, so I also didn't love that the hub needed to be plugged in constantly for the device to work. But most of all, I don't think the device is accurately measuring activity metrics.
Is a Smart Tracker Worth It for Your Cat?
According to the American Veterinary Medical Association, about 10 million cats and dogs go missing each year in the US. While smart trackers aren't a silver bullet for preventing that problem, the data they provide can be helpful. Sure, you could technically use an Apple AirTag to track your cat—as I did for many years with Basil—but you'd have to hope it’s in range in an urgent situation. These smart health and GPS trackers are more accurate and alert you if your cat has escaped the “safe zone”—aka your home—especially helpful for indoor-only cats like mine. If your cat is indoor-outdoor, helpful heat maps trace regular routes, and you can add multiple safe zones so if your kitty ventures too far, you'll still be alerted. No matter which type of cat you have, these trackers allow you to follow your pet in real time when it matters most.
Plus, the health monitoring intel helps you better understand your pet's needs, routines, and normal patterns. Historical data comparisons can help identify warning signs of potential health issues, such as increased sleep or decreased activity.
There is a cost, though: A combination GPS tracker and smart health collar requires a subscription plan (see the individual reviews for more detail on rates), which is more expensive than a general tracker with no subscription required, like an AirTag. These smart trackers also require maintenance, such as frequent charging, firmware updates, and in-app monitoring. But I like to think of the devices as insurance—you hope you'll never need to rely on one, but in the event of an emergency, you'll be glad you invested. (Plus, it's fun to track your pet's metrics and understand a little more about their inner world.)

New Delhi, December 1975. It was love at first sight when a Swedish hippy called Lotta von Schedvin sat down to be sketched by an Indian street artist, Pradyumna Kumar Mahanandia, known to everyone as PK. In the 10 minutes it took PK to complete her portrait, everything clicked into place for the pair. They were swept headlong in a whirlwind romance, and PK took Lotta to his village in the east of India to meet his family. But soon after, the time came for Lotta to pack up her VW campervan and head back home with her friends.
Heart-stricken PK promised to follow, but a plane ticket to Sweden was an impossible dream. Determined not to lose the love of his life, PK bought a secondhand Raleigh bike, and with $80 sewn into the waistband of his trousers, set off to cycle 6,000 miles to Lotta. He knew the sun set in the west, so that was the direction he took. His plan was to follow the hippy trail, cycling through India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Iran and Turkey, crossing Europe, finally arriving in Sweden.
Actually, he was heading to Switzerland until a fellow backpacker pointed out that Switzerland and Sweden were two different countries. In a new Netflix documentary, The Cycle of Love, PK jokes that his strength was his fuzzy grasp of European geography. Watching the film, you wonder if his superpower might have been his smile – warm and joyous, it lights the room. Either way, he made it to Sweden. The journey took 123 days, and ended up involving a flight or two, and a couple of trains. In May 1977, PK knocked on Lotta’s door in Borås, Sweden. They have been together ever since.
Documentary-maker Orlando von Einsiedel first heard about the story when he gave a talk in Sweden. “At the end, two young people came up and handed me a book,” he says. “They said: ‘This is about our parents’ story. We know your work. Would you be interested in this as a film?’” The book was The Amazing Story of the Man Who Cycled from India to Europe for Love by Swedish journalist Per J Andersson.
The two young people were PK and Lotta’s grownup kids Emilie and Karl. Von Einsiedel politely took the book but didn’t think too much about it. “Normally in my experience, when somebody approaches you and says ‘I’ve got a brilliant story’, it doesn’t work out.”
A couple of months later, Von Einsiedel picked up the book as a holiday read, opening it on the flight out of London. “The moment I started I thought, ‘Oh my God, you idiot Orlando! This is extraordinary.’” It wasn’t just the against-all-odds, 6,000-mile cycle ride, PK’s story was a tale of fate and destiny. When he was born, the astrologer in his village made four predictions about his future wife: she would be a Taurus, born outside India, musical and own a jungle. So naturally the first question he asked Lotta was: “Are you a Taurus?” Her answer was yes. She was also a gifted musician, and – most bonkers of all – her family owned land with a forest in Sweden.
“When you tell people the story, it’s almost too good to be true,” says Von Einsiedel, cheerful and chatty on a video call from New York. The previous night he attended the US premiere of The Cycle of Love with PK and Lotta, who have been happily married for nearly 50 years. The pair have been getting the celebrity treatment wherever they go. “Everybody in the cinema stands up for them, people are weeping when they come on stage.” What do the couple make of the film? He grins. “I know they like it, because whenever they go to a festival, they watch every single screening from beginning to end.” How many times have they seen it? “A lot.”
The film tells their story with enormous warmth. It includes a dramatisation of the epic ride, with PK played by the British-based Indian actor Chirag Lobo, and Mina Dale as Lotta. Everybody else is non-professional, explains Von Einsiedel. “Our producers would go out and street-cast people on the morning of filming.”
What about the script, I ask? There are gorgeous, heartwarming scenes as PK shares his story with people he meets on the road, who in return tell him about their life and loves. How were those scenes scripted? “No script. Everything is improvised. When PK interacts with everyday people he meets along the way, those are just normal conversations about love and hopes and dreams.”
Wasn’t that a bit risky – getting a plane to India with two actors, no script and trusting that deep and meaningful conversations would materialise from conversations with ordinary people? “Massively risky, except I tested if it might work in Lewisham town centre,” Von Einsiedel says, grinning. “I have a friend who’s an actor. We went to Lewisham with a bike.” Armed with a notepad, his friend told people that he was cycling from London to Cape Town for love. “He pretended to draw portraits. What was extraordinary is the first person he sat down to draw turned around and said: ‘I love your story. I’ll buy you a plane ticket immediately.’”
It’s the kindness of strangers that makes the documentary so uplifting. When PK cycles out of Kabul, he stops to help an Austrian backpacker, Linea, who crashed her car, knocking out most of her teeth. He stays with her for several days at hospital, even though it means his visa expiring and further delay. Later, when he arrives in Istanbul and checks his post, there is a train ticket to Vienna – a thank you from Linea for his kindness.
What struck Von Einsiedel when he met the real-life PK was that his story about love went beyond boy-meets-girl. “For me, it’s not just about romantic love. It’s about self-love and love for all the people that we share this planet with.” PK was born into a dalit family, the marginalised group in India formerly known as “untouchables”. At school, he was made to sit outside during lessons and not allowed to play with the other children. Even after he won a scholarship to study fine art in Delhi, he experienced periods of homelessness and isolation.
“From the moment I started talking to PK it became clear what a difficult and traumatic childhood he’d had,” Von Einsiedel says. “He spoke so movingly about being on the journey and how it was the first time that strangers would touch him and hug him. That it was key to him starting to believe in himself and love himself. He said: ‘How can you love anybody if you can’t love yourself?’ I get emotional just saying that.”
PK explained how he felt accepted on the journey, hanging out with hippies and locals in the villages and towns he passed through. People with very little offered him hospitality, a meal or a roof for the night. In the documentary, this warm feeling of togetherness thuds to the ground when PK arrives in Europe, grilled by hostile and overtly racist German border officers. “That was his first experience,” says Von Einsiedel. “He travelled through all these countries, Afghanistan and Iran, and everybody treated him with respect. Then as soon as he got to Europe he immediately experienced racism.”
Von Einsiedel grew up in south London. At university he studied social anthropology and in his 20s was a professional snowboarder. “I learned the craft of film-making making snowboard films,” he says. “When I knew how to do that, I segued into making films about social issues I believed in.” He started working with Al Jazeera, travelling to conflict zones.
In 2015, he was nominated for an Oscar for his first full-length documentary, Virunga, about the battle to save a national park in eastern Congo, home to some of the world’s last mountain gorillas. His documentary short, White Helmets, following Syrian volunteers rescuing civilians, won an Oscar. Next he made Evelyn, an incredibly moving film in which Von Einsiedel turned the camera on his own family. His brother Evelyn took his own life aged 22 over a decade earlier. In the film, Von Einsiedel and his two surviving siblings hiked the routes their brother loved to walk with friends and family. “I was very emotionally closed for a long time after my brother died,” he says. “I used to think being emotionally open was a sign of weakness. I was terrified of my own emotions. I see the opposite now. I think being emotionally open is a sign of strength.”
When it comes to picking a subject for a new documentary, he says he is attracted to people who inspire him. “I’m drawn to stories that show the better side of human beings. That’s a thread that runs through the work I like to make.” The Cycle of Love is by far the sunniest film he has made to date. What’s that all about, I ask? “I wanted to make an optimistic film that’s about joy and human connection. The world is difficult. Love is one of those things that all of us can agree on. This story just felt so important to tell.”

A ‘Wall of Hope’, a youth-led initiative by the Schizophrenia Research Foundation (SCARF) and its Department of Youth Mental Health, was unveiled at the IIT-Madras Research Park in Taramani on Saturday, a press release said.
With young people facing increasing mental health challenges and suicide remaining concern, creating spaces for expression, connection, resilience, and help-seeking is vital.
The mental health campaign, which began on October 10, 2025, encourages young people aged 10-25 to express, share, and reflect upon their personal reasons for living, through brief messages of hope.
Adolescents and young adults across the country were invited to write the purpose of life on colourful post-it notes.
The activity is completely youth-led through peer leaders and trainer modules, where young people played a central role in leading and facilitating the campaign.
More than 20,000 responses from across six States have been collected.
Additionally, 400 volunteers have been trained to conduct this activity, which is voluntary and anonymous, to initiate and foster conversations around mental health.
Justice N. Anand Venkatesh, Madras High Court judge, and Lakshmi Vijayakumar, founder of suicide prevention organisation SNEHA, participated in the event, besides SCARF vice-chairperson R. Thara and director Sridhar Vaitheswaran.
(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, and Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050)

In late 1970, a Titan IIIC rocket launched from Space Launch Complex 40 at what was then called Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. It carried a top-secret payload for the US military.
Much has changed in spaceflight since then. The Titan IIIC would bow out in 1982 after dozens of launches. Various Titans continued launching from Space Launch Complex 40 until 2005, at which point the US Air Force—in a competitive process hotly opposed by United Launch Alliance—turned the pad over to a small, largely unknown startup called SpaceX. And Cape Canaveral is now a “Space Force” station.
But those unspecified payloads? Until last month, some of them were still flying operationally.
They were looking for missile launches
The US government would later disclose that the top-secret payload that launched in November 1970 was a “Defense Support Program” satellite. The initial block of these satellites, launched from 1970 to 1973, had a mass of about 1 metric ton, and each carried about 2,000 infrared detectors. They were essentially very sensitive telescopes, and each satellite was launched into geosynchronous orbit.
For a time, these were among the most important satellites flown by the US, as they served to detect the launch of a nuclear warhead at the country. As a result, the Defense Support Program would become one of the primary elements of American military space power during the Cold War.
These initial satellites transformed experimental infrared observations into an operational program that continuously monitored the globe for missile launches. Initially built to identify Soviet ICBMs, they were essential for nuclear deterrence; later, they also became useful in conventional warfare, such as detecting Iraqi Scud missile launches.
Over time, the military added to the constellation, improving reliability and expanding their capabilities. Each satellite ended up having more than 6,000 infrared detectors and a mass of about 2.5 tons. Satellites in the Defense Support Program kept on flying into space until 2007. One of them, DSP-16, even launched on a space shuttle (Atlantis) in 1991.

The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has claimed he is the only thing standing in the way of far-right “fascists” reclaiming power, as he led a huge rally through the streets of Rio ahead of Sunday’s crunch election.
Speaking on the eve of the demonstration, the 80-year-old leftwinger said he had decided to seek a historic fourth term because he believed only he could prevent the family of his rightwing rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, returning to government.
“If it weren’t for me standing up to these fascists they’d easily win another election. I’m the one standing in their way,” Lula told a popular podcast called Flow, before adding: “It’s either me, or it’s barbarism.”
Hours later, Lula flew to Rio, staging what his team called a “victory march” between two highly symbolic downtown locations that played an important role in Brazil’s fight for democracy during the 1964-1985 military dictatorship.
“What’s at stake is not the victory of one man, it is the victory of an idea, it’s the victory of democracy,” Brazil’s president said after the parade set off from the Candelária church. The church is the location where more than a million people, including Lula, famously gathered in 1984 to demand direct presidential elections.
Lula, who was among those who spoke at that historic demo when he was an up-and-coming politician in his 30s, added: “Either we consolidate democracy, or we will lose it.”
From Candelária, a sea of red-clad Lula supporters marched a mile south towards Cinelândia, the scene of an equally well-known pro-democracy protest in 1968 called the March of the Hundred Thousand.
“No gringo is going to lay a finger on Brazil’s things,” vowed Lula, in an indirect reference to claims Donald Trump’s administration is seeking to sway the vote in Bolsonaro’s favour with a campaign of economic and diplomatic pressure.
The decision to hold Friday’s rally between two such politically charged places spoke to how this year’s election has stirred up renewed fears over the future of Latin America’s biggest democracy.
Election-eve polls suggest Lula holds only a slender lead over his adversary, whose father, the ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a failed coup after Lula beat him in the 2022 election.
Many Brazilian democrats fear that if 45-year-old Bolsonaro wins this year’s election, he will move quickly to free his father and his fellow coup-plotters from jail – and then set about dismantling and co-opting the country’s democratic institutions, such as the supreme court.
“This is the most important election of our lives – and we have to do everything we can to win,” said Marcelo Freixo, a politician from Lula’s Worker’s party (PT) who is running for a seat in congress.
Freixo warned: “We spent 21 years living under a really harsh dictatorship. We fought so hard to attain our democratic institutions. And a victory for the Bolsonaro family – a family that always … openly defended the dictatorship and tried to stage a coup … would spell the end for our democratic process and institutions.”
Valmir Aleixo, a 55-year-old history teacher who was one of thousands of people who joined Friday’s pro-Lula demo, said: “This is [a choice] between democracy and the savagery of far-right fascism. This is perhaps the most important election since the return of democracy in the 80s.”
Noni Ostrower, 74, came to what was Rio’s largest leftwing protest in years carrying a homemade banner that read: “Democracy Is Valuable”.
“I’m the daughter of two refugees from nazism. They came to Brazil from Germany because of this,” Ostrower said. “I was born here in Brazil … and today I have grandchildren and I absolutely do not want to see fascism return to Brazil – it would be a tragedy for the country. That’s why I’m here today.”
During the campaign, Flávio Bolsonaro has vowed to pardon his 71-year-old father if elected, with some speculating Jair Bolsonaro could even become a minister. His brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, a radical former congressman with ties to Trump’s Maga movement, reputedly hopes to become foreign minister. Flávio Bolsonaro has announced plans to appoint five firmly conservative supreme court judges.
Luiz Eduardo Soares, a prominent anthropologist and writer, said he feared what might happen if the Bolsonaro clan managed to reclaim power.
“I think these elections could be the last ones in my life, for my generation … What was done over the course of 10 years in Hungary, [Bolsonaro] will do in two,” Soares predicted in reference to the European country’s transformation into an “electoral autocracy” under its former prime minister, Viktor Orbán.
Diogo Nogueira, a famous samba singer who came to the rally wearing his trademark panama hat, said: “We need to win in the first round so we don’t allow this type of people to get back into government. If they do get back in, it won’t just be a problem for four years, but for 10 or 20.”
Polls suggest the election is likely to go to a second round runoff between Lula and Bolsonaro on 25 October, with Lula expected to secure about 45% of votes on Sunday and Bolsonaro 40%, according to the Datafolha pollster. But at Friday’s rally Lula claimed he could pull off a shock first-round win by claiming more than 50% of the vote.
In an online broadcast, Bolsonaro insisted his campaign would prevail. “Brazil is a few hours from deciding its future … for the next 30, 40, 50 years. It’s the end of an era. It’s the end of the Worker’s party era,” he claimed, asking undecided voters to back him to achieve that aim, even if they didn’t like him.

The Diabetic Foot Society of India (DFSI), under the aegis of its national president V.B. Narayanamurthy, has written to Zulfiqarali G. Abbas, president of the Pan-African Diabetic Foot Study Group (PADFSG), proposing the formation of a global alliance on diabetic foot survival and limb preservation.
The letter, a copy of which was shared with The Hindu, notes that diabetic foot ulceration is an under-recognised cause of premature death, major amputation, recurrent illness, disability, and social exclusion. Available evidence shows that its five-year mortality is comparable to that of some cancers. And yet, global investment, policy attention, organised pathways, and post-amputation support remain substantially below the scale of the problem, the letter notes.
The DFSI, therefore, has proposed that institutions, including itself, King’s College London, International Association of Diabetic Foot Surgeons, D-Foot International, American Limb Preservation Society, Federation of International Podiatrists, and PADFSG, come together to form a Global Alliance for Diabetic Foot Survival and Limb Preservation, to create a sustained, scientific, and policy platform for prevention, limb preservation, improved survival, rehabilitation, surveillance, research, and engagement with governments and the World Health Organization (WHO).
The letter further stated that DFSI would announce the shared intention to form the Alliance at its next national conference, slated to be held on October 2, 2026. This, it said, would be an announcement of intent rather than a representation that the Alliance had been legally constituted or that any institution had accepted a financial or contractual obligation.
The letter urged the PADFSG to provide in-principle concurrence with the formation of the Alliance and the proposed conference announcement.
Apart from the proposal for the alliance, the letter also contained a draft Joint Global Declaration for joint consultation and unveiling, and asked for comments on the proposal and draft declaration from the PADFSG.
The DAFSI also stated that subject to the PADFSG’s concurrence, it proposed to convene the first founding meeting of the Alliance within 30 days of its conference.
The proposal
The proposal noted that the Alliance would provide a common platform for scientific leadership, policy advocacy, regional demonstration programmes, and responsible resource mobilisation. Its objectives would include advocacy with the WHO and national governments to secure explicit recognition of diabetic foot disease as an important medical condition; to improve survival and quality of life through multi-disciplinary care and patient-centred research; to promote prevention, early detection, and rapid referral; to advance surveillance and support the development of registries; to strengthen post-amputation rehabilitation; to promote research and training programmes; and to ensure the meaningful participation of people living with diabetes in governance and programme design.
The proposal also detailed membership and governance, standing bodies, the Secretariat, proposed activities of the Alliance, donor engagement, and financial management, as well as a performance framework and a risks safeguard.
The declaration
The draft declaration called for diabetic foot disease to be recognised as a major cause of premature death, disability, and exclusion. It called upon the WHO Director-General, regional directors, and member states to make diabetic foot prevention, limb preservation and survival a visible part of diabetes policy, establish common indicators and baseline registries, and support flagship programmes in at least two WHO regions.
It also proposed a goal to reduce risk-adjusted five-year mortality after a new diabetic foot ulcer by 30%, and potentially avoidable major amputations by 50% by 2030.
The draft declaration called for coordinated action that keeps people alive, mobile, included, and able to live with dignity.

Bitchat, the decentralised messaging platform founded by Twitter (now X) cofounder Jack Dorsey, has been removed from Google Play Store and Apple’s App Store following an official government order. In a post on X, Dorsey shared an official email from Apple, which read that the IT ministry (MeitY) had issued directions for the removal of the Bitchat app from the App Store under Section 69A of the IT Act. The email noted that the app allegedly included content deemed illegal in India. However, the communique did not specify what content had triggered the takedown order. Apple advised the developer to seek further details from MeitY directly. The Apple email further noted that Bitchat’s beta-testing access via TestFlight has also been blocked. However, the app would remain available on its App Store outside India. Meanwhile, Bitchat is no longer available for download via the Google Play Store as well and its website also appears to no longer be accessible in the country. It’s unclear whether this is for the same reason. Launched by Dorsey in 2025, Bitchat is an open-source messaging app that enables peer-to-peer (P2) communication through Bluetooth mesh networks without requiring internet access or centralised servers. The app does not require users to make accounts and has no central identity system either. It can be used during extreme occasions like internet outages and natural disasters, or in areas with poor network coverage. This is not the first time that Bitchat has landed in choppy regulatory waters in the country. In July this year, Dorsey had claimed the Indian government had directed GitHub to remove multiple repositories linked to Bitchat. He had shared a notification issued by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to support his claims. The I4C’s notification had raised concerns that Bitchat’s implementation of anonymous communication prevents authorities from obtaining subscriber details or communication records during active investigations. The agency also warned that the platform could be exploited to evade surveillance and bypass internet shutdowns to coordinate unlawful assemblies, protests, or criminal activities. Notably, I4C’s concerns had come amid the unrest over the NEET 2026 paper leak, when protesters were reportedly using Bitchat to communicate amid suspension of mobile internet services at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The action against Bitchat appears to be a part of Centre’s broader plan to tighten scrutiny of social media platforms. Earlier this year, MeitY had proposed amendments to the IT Rules, 2021, which would make government advisories legally binding on online intermediaries. The draft rules also proposed requiring platforms to remove content that could be used to commit unlawful acts within three hours of receiving a court order or a reasoned government notice.

Going ‘car-lite’: why more Singaporeans are quitting driving
Rail links and cycle routes make it easier for motorists to give up their cars as running costs and road charges rise
Instead, the 49-year-old business consultant decided in May to go without a car for the first time in two decades.
High COE prices, rising running costs and the hassle of parking and congestion are prompting more Singaporeans to reconsider car ownership, as the land-scarce city state expands public transport, cycling infrastructure and other alternatives in a push for a more “car-lite” society.

ఈ నేపథ్యంలో, బీహార్లోని జముయ్లో జరిగిన వేధింపుల ఘటనలో నిందితులను పోలీసులు అరెస్ట్ చేస్తున్న దృశ్యాలు అంటూ కొన్ని వీడియోలను సోషల్ మీడియాలో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు. ఈ వీడియోల వెనుక ఉన్న నిజానిజాలను ఈ కథనంలో పరిశీలిద్దాం.

వార్తా కథనంలో ముఖాలను కప్పి ఉంచిన ముగ్గురు నిందితులు ధరించిన దుస్తులు, వైరల్ వీడియోలో కనిపిస్తున్న దుస్తులతో సరిపోలుతున్నాయి. దీంతో ఈ వీడియో అదే ఘటనకు సంబంధించినదని నిర్ధారించవచ్చు.
చివరిగా, మధ్యప్రదేశ్లోని అలీరాజ్పూర్కు సంబంధించిన వీడియోను జముయ్ ఘటనలో నిందితులను పోలీసులు అరెస్ట్ చేస్తున్న దృశ్యాలు అంటూ షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు.

Nagoya – Taiwanese boxer Lin Yu-ting won a “monumental” Asian Games gold on Friday and said she was “grateful for making it through” after considering quitting following a major gender row at the Paris Olympics.
The 30-year-old beat China’s Yang Chengyu 5-0 in the women’s 60-kilogram final in Nagoya, giving her a second Asian Games gold after winning in the 57-kg class in Hangzhou three years ago.
Lin said before the Games that she had considered retiring after winning gold at the Paris Olympics but wanted to carry on fighting in part to defy those who questioned her eligibility.
She said after her victory in Nagoya that she had been “waiting for that moment when the light breaks through“.
“It was really not easy at all,” she said.
“It’s rare to finally reach that point where you see the dawn, and I’m just so grateful to myself for making it through.”
Lin and Imane Khelif of Algeria found themselves in the middle of a major gender row at the 2024 Olympics, with U.S. President Donald Trump, Elon Musk and author J.K. Rowling among those wading in.
The two boxers had been disqualified from the 2023 world championships by the International Boxing Association (IBA) after the organisation said they failed unspecified gender eligibility tests.
However, the IOC allowed them to compete in Paris, saying they were victims of “a sudden and arbitrary decision” by the widely discredited IBA. Both went on to win gold.
’Not afraid to die’
Lin said winning at the Asian Games was different from her Olympic victory, adding that its “significance is monumental“.
“I basically just felt like packing up my things and rushing back home — that was the kind of mindset I had,” she said of past experience.
“I didn’t hold on to any hope any more. I am so grateful to the coach for always believing in me and always believing that good things would happen.”
Lin was backed by a small pocket of vocal Taiwanese supporters in the cosy Nishio Gymnasium.
Towering over her opponent, she used her superior reach to take control of the bout and had a clear advantage heading into the third and final round.
She held off a late assault from Yang to take gold, celebrating with the minimum of fuss.
Lin said she decided to compete in a heavier weight class at the Asian Games because she was “not afraid to die“.
“People are like that — you want to see a different version of yourself,” she said.
“Since I already had a really solid track record at 57kg, I also wanted to give myself a different challenge and see just how far I could go.”
Lin refused to confirm whether she planned to defend her Olympic title at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
“I believe that in the future, we can also put on an even better performance, persevere all the way and laugh until the end,” she said.

Although Digger has premiered this weekend to mixed reviews, Guillermo Del Toro is a confirmed fan of the Alejandro G. Iñárritu satire.
The 3x Oscar winner has taken to social media to heap praise on Tom Cruise‘s latest after responding to a critic that called the film “far from a must-watch” and recommended viewers wait for it to hit streaming.
“Entirely Petty headline,” wrote Del Toro in response to IGN’s review. “Love it or not. And, yes, I do. The film delivers in scale, ambition and reach at a theatrical screen level. Daring, bold and cinematically complex. Decidedly a theatrical experience.”
It turns out the algorithm was listening, as the Pan’s Labyrinth auteur has since continued reposting other fans’ praise of the Warner Bros. movie, which is now in theaters.
Watch on Deadline
“Funny, I go into the platform and without even scrolling down, these are popping at the top of my timeline…” he wrote with one repost. “So… I will just keep posting them. Tune in or drop out-“
“Dig or Die – c’mon!” Del Toro wrote with another.
Sitting at a 51% critic rating on Rotten Tomatoes with a C+ CinemaScore, Del Toro compared the bad reviews for Digger to the criticism that surrounded The King of Comedy (1982), The Big Lebowski (1998) and The Counselor (2013), all having since become appreciated by audiences years later.
In Digger, Cruise stars as the titular oil tycoon Digger Rockwell, who races to fix a catastrophe he caused so he can avoid blame and be seen as humanity’s savior.

NEW DELHI: India's role in efforts to find a negotiated end to the Russia-Ukraine war has gained greater prominence, with Kyiv describing an Indian proposal as the most comprehensive among four initiatives currently under discussion and saying New Delhi has, for the first time, indicated its willingness to play an active mediating role.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha recently said Ukraine was prepared to consider both an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while also remaining open to an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact."We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is India's proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role," Sybiha said during a press briefing, according to RBC Ukraine.
India proposal among four initiatives
According to Sybiha, four proposals are currently being considered in diplomatic efforts surrounding the war.India's proposal was described by the Ukrainian foreign minister as the most comprehensive.Türkiye and Egypt have separately proposed a grain and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while the United States has put forward an energy truce proposal.The agricultural and maritime component is particularly important for Egypt, which relies on Ukrainian grain for roughly a third of its supply, according to RBC Ukraine.
The US proposal on an energy truce was also discussed during a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump.Kyiv has conveyed its own approach to its partners and wants the energy and Black Sea components to be treated as an interconnected package.Sybiha said the energy component would require a complete halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, including port facilities.Ukraine has also expressed readiness for an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Sybiha said such a ceasefire could potentially emerge from a meeting between Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The US is currently working actively on this diplomatic track, according to the Ukrainian foreign minister.
Kyiv backs safe Black Sea shipping
The latest Ukrainian position builds on India's earlier engagement with Kyiv over restoring safe navigation in the Black Sea.During last month's UN General Assembly-related engagements, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Türkiye had put forward options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine."We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere," Zelenskyy said at the time.Also read:India's proposal under consideration for safe Black Sea shipping, Zelenskyy saysIndia has been engaging with both Moscow and Kyiv while advocating dialogue and diplomacy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had said India was in continuous contact with both sides and was exploring ideas that could help mitigate and eventually end the conflict."If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there," Jaishankar said during his visit to Kyiv last month.During that visit, Jaishankar met Zelenskyy and Sybiha, with discussions covering peace efforts, bilateral cooperation, Black Sea navigation and global food security.Sybiha had also said Ukraine valued India's engagement in efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea."Restoring freedom of navigation is critical for global food security. Ukraine is ready to play a constructive role and we value India’s engagement," he said in a post on X.
Russia's position remains key to next steps
While Ukraine has indicated its readiness to consider multiple limited ceasefire arrangements, Russia's response remains central to whether the proposals can move forward.Sybiha's comments come amid differing assessments in Europe over Moscow's willingness to enter substantive peace negotiations.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz recently said Russia was not currently interested in genuine peace negotiations, while German foreign minister Johann Wadephul has expressed expectations that talks to end the war could begin in the near future.
The Kremlin had previously said there were no prerequisites for moving towards a broader peace negotiating track while maintaining that Russia remained open to talks."For now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.Ukraine's latest position therefore places several limited ceasefire proposals, covering energy infrastructure, Black Sea shipping and agricultural supplies, alongside the possibility of a broader unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact.India's proposal is being considered alongside those initiatives, with Sybiha describing it as the most comprehensive and saying New Delhi has now signalled its readiness to play a role in the process.

Srinagar, Sep 22: The ongoing Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly session has come under criticism from All Party Sikh Coordination Committee Chairman and senior political leader Jagmohan Singh Raina, who alleged that the House is spending more time on political confrontations and Jammu-versus-Kashmir rhetoric than on issues directly affecting the public.
The Assembly witnessed uproar over the cancellation of the December 5 holiday commemorating the birth anniversary of Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, founder and leader of the National Conference. During the proceedings, questions were also raised over the continuation of the holiday marking the birth anniversary of Maharaja Hari Singh, with demands for its cancellation as well.
Reacting to the developments, Raina, as per a statement issued on Tuesday, said people elect legislators with the expectation that their problems will be raised in the Assembly, debated and followed by concrete efforts to find solutions.
He questioned why legislators were engaging in political confrontation instead of using the Assembly to bring resolutions on issues affecting ordinary citizens.
Raina also expressed concern over what he described as increasing Jammu-versus-Kashmir rhetoric inside the House. He said issues surrounding Article 370 and Article 35A should not overshadow the pressing concerns for which people expect their elected representatives to work.
According to Raina, the Assembly should give greater attention to unemployment, vacant posts in the health sector, shortage of doctors and paramedical staff, and vacancies in educational institutions.
He alleged that thousands of posts remain vacant across different departments and questioned whether the government has a clear long-term strategy to address unemployment and staffing shortages, particularly in healthcare and education.
Raina said every MLA should use the Assembly platform to highlight problems faced by people in their respective constituencies and seek practical solutions.
He also referred to earlier Assemblies, saying that, in his view, legislators had maintained greater decorum and devoted more attention to government programmes, policies and public welfare.

(Representative image): Registrar Nisar Ahmad Mir said he had spoken to the protesting students and assured them that anyone using 'such language' should be reported to university authorities immediately.
SRINAGAR: Central University of Kashmir has removed chemistry department head Chinnappan Baskar after some female students accused him of harassing them and asking one of them out on a “date”.“Pending an inquiry into the complaint, Chinnappan Baskar is attached with the office of dean (academic affairs) with immediate effect and relieved of all official assignments,” an order issued by the varsity’s deputy registrar stated.
Scores of students had protested against Baskar on Thursday, accusing him of passing “lewd remarks” at female students, telling one of them she was becoming “more beautiful with each passing day” before asking her out on a date. The protesters also alleged that Baskar threatened to “destroy” their careers.Registrar Nisar Ahmad Mir said he had spoken to the protesting students and assured them that anyone using “such language” should be reported to university authorities immediately. He quoted the students as saying that Baskar used “abusive language in the class.”“We brought the matter to the notice of the vice-chancellor, who ordered his attachment and an inquiry,” Mir said. He claimed this was the first such complaint officially made to varsity officials.In a statement on Saturday, the university reaffirmed its zero-tolerance policy on sexual harassment, assuring complainants confidentiality and action under the 2013 Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act.

Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.
Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.
Meanwhile, heavy rainfall in Nepal last week resulted in 542 disaster incidents and left 27 people dead between 24 and 27 September, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Of the recorded incidents, 304 were related to landslides while 87 were linked to flooding.
During this extremely wet period, 186 meteorological sites recorded more than 100mm of rainfall, with Dedhgaun, in Lumbini province, recording 544.2mm. Nearly a million people received SMS flood warnings, and 2,000 people living in high-risk areas were relocated.
This heavy rainfall also affected the Gandak River in Bihar, north-east India, which reached a record water level of 91.25 metres on Tuesday, 0.35m metres above the previous record, set only in 2024, according to the water resources department. So far, 169 seepage points along the embankments have been repaired, with teams deployed across several sites along the river as the embankments continue to face heavy water pressure.
Strong winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding have hit the north-east US as a very deep area of low pressure developed into a nor’easter on Saturday. Such storms are named due to the north-easterly winds typically affecting coastal areas. This was the first nor’easter of the autumn and winter season, bringing gusts of up to 74mph (119km/h) and waves rising to 3 metres.
The storm left approximately 200,000 people without power, inundated the streets of New York City and killed one person when a tree fell in Brooklyn. However, the storm also uncovered a piece of history as the wreckage from the Warren Sawyer, a three-masted ship destroyed in 1884, washed ashore on Nantucket, off Cape Cod in Massachusetts.

The Pentagon is informing more than 2 million current and former military members that their personnel records storing sensitive personal information were stolen over a monthslong compromise of one of its networks. The breach is the second one in recent months to expose sensitive government information.
The records, according to one notification letter posted to Reddit, included Social Security numbers, names, addresses, sex, race, and occupational specialty. This last category could be particularly valuable to foreign adversaries because it could help their intelligence agencies in identifying high-value military personnel. Starting last October, hackers gained access to a system operated by the Defense Manpower Data Center, which collates Department of Defense personnel records. The Pentagon says that the breach compromised the records of 2.8 million living individuals.
A potential boon
The incident is the second time a major network breach in recent months has exposed sensitive US government personnel records that criminal groups or foreign adversaries could use. Last month, the ransomware group ShinyHunters claimed it hacked into FBI systems and stole records of thousands of the agency’s current or former employees. Reuters reported the job titles in the records included ones related to investigating China or Russia.
ShinyHunters said that it has no plans to release the information, but the promises of a criminal organization that has hacked and extorted hundreds of organizations mean very little. Additionally, the group’s cyber defenses are likely no match against nation-state intelligence hackers. An FBI official this week called on group members to turn themselves in.

Singapore’s sailors conclude Asian Games campaign with three silvers, one bronze
This marks the first Games in 24 years where the sailors have gone without a gold.
NAGOYA: Singapore’s sailing team added two more Asian Games medals to their haul on Saturday (Oct 3), concluding their campaign with three silvers and one bronze.
All four medals were secured by Games debutants.
At the Kaiyoh Yacht Harbor, Ian Goh clinched silver in the boys’ ILCA 4 after amassing 25 net points from 12 races. Goh finished level with South Korea's Choi Jiun, but missed out on gold as he had one less first-place finish than his rival. Hong Kong’s Tiago Salgado took bronze.
At the last edition of the Asiad, Ian’s brother Isaac also took silver in the same event.
In the boys’ windsurfing event, John Wong finished with the bronze medal, the sailing team's first bronze at the Games. Hong Kong's Wong Tsz Ho won gold, and Japan's Masato Kozono finished in second.
Earlier on Friday, Jania Ang (Women’s ILCA 6) as well as Nigel Tan and Sean Kum (Boys’ 29er) claimed silvers in their respective events.
This marks the first Games in 24 years where the sailors have gone without a gold.
At the 2022 Games, Singapore’s sailors won two golds, two silvers and three bronze medals in Ningbo, with Maximilian Maeder (men’s formula kite) and Ryan Lo (men’s ILCA 7) winning their events.

Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka both struck twice as England ran riot in a 7-0 rout of abject Croatia in the Nations League on Saturday.
Thomas Tuchel’s side ripped Croatia to shreds in Rijeka to make it two wins from its first three matches in its Nations League group.
England captain Kane’s double extended his record goal tally for his country to 89. But the Bayern Munich striker was far from the only standout performer for England. Arsenal winger Saka also bagged a brace as England recorded the biggest win of the Tuchel era.
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham, restored to the starting line-up after Tuesday’s 2-0 win against Czech Republic, was on target to cap a vibrant display featuring three assists.
The effervescent Anthony Gordon netted to make it four goals in his last four England matches before Morgan Rogers completed the annihilation.
Chasing a top-two finish to secure a spot in the Nations League quarterfinals in March, England concluded the international break against Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday.
That should be a slightly more raucous occasion than this tie, which was played ‘behind closed doors’ because of crowd trouble involving Croatia fans against France in 2025.
ALSO READ | Ronaldo will always be Portugal’s biggest icon: Bruno Fernandes calls for unity amidst controversy
Around 6,000 local school children and 100 England supporters were allowed into the Stadion HNK Rijeka, creating a subdued environment in a country known for its hostile atmospheres.
Tuchel’s men took just eight minutes to go ahead with an incisive raid that exposed the talent gap between the side. Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, making his first start for England, was the catalyst with a composed pass to Bellingham.
Bellingham slipped an equally measured ball in behind the flat-footed Croatia defence, and Kane took a deft touch before stroking a clinical finish into the roof of the net from 10 yards.
England had too much pace and poise for Croatia, and it was no surprise when Bellingham increased its advantage at the end of a flowing 27-pass move in the 21st minute.
Saka’s cross was too high for his teammates, but Gordon adroitly controlled the ball in mid-air and whipped it back into the six-yard box, where Bellingham stretched to poke into the far corner.
Gordon put the result beyond doubt in the 39th minute, diving to meet Jarell Quansah’s pinpoint cross with an agile header that flashed past Dominik Livakovic from six yards.
Bellingham was in an irrepressible mood, driving into the Croatia area and baffling Luka Modric with a smooth drag-back before crossing low towards Saka, who slotted home from close range on the stroke of half-time.
England showed no mercy after the interval, and Kane netted again in the 53rd minute, sliding in to convert Anderson’s cross with ease.
Saka got the sixth from Kane’s pass after another woeful error from hapless Croatia in the 68th minute.
Rogers came off the bench to put the seal on England’s swaggering display, rounding Livakovic to net from Bellingham’s 87th-minute pass.

President Donald Trump’s new assistant press secretary — a former reporter for Real America's Voice — once posed for a photo with a rifle while wearing a "f*** Joe Biden" T-shirt and was a fan of slain conservative influencer Charlie Kirk.
Beni Rae Harmony, 24, announced on Friday that she will join Trump's White House press team as the new assistant press secretary. Anti-MAGA accounts on Instagram quickly found the photo of Harmony in her anti-Biden shirt, according to The Daily Beast.
The photo was posted by former Republican Virginia congressional candidate Jarome Bell in 2021. The post includes the caption "My campaign Public Affairs Director @beniraeharmony is a beast. This is how we roll."
Harmony's Instagram account liked the post. Bell ran for Congress in 2022 in Virginia Beach.
Harmony will join the White House's communications team following a staff shakeup that included the departure of former Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt in August.
"It's been an honor to report, travel, and cover this historic administration as Senior White House Correspondent for Real America's Voice. My goal has always been to ask questions that matter to real Americans and make sure their voices are heard," Harmony wrote in a post announcing her hiring. "I'm incredibly grateful to President Trump for this opportunity and his trust."
Harmony formerly worked for the far-right broadcaster Real America's Voice, which always airs Steve Bannon's weekday show, The Charlie Kirk Show, and Ted Nugent's Spirit Campfire.

Harmony defended her decision to air the memorial, calling it "non-partisan."
She previously worked at Kirk's Turning Point USA conservative youth organization in 2020 and 2021. Harmony said she considered Kirk a "mentor."
Her LinkedIn profile says she also interned for Arizona Republican Congressman Paul Gosar and former Florida Congressman Matt Gaetz.
Harmony may have caught Trump's eye during a trip to Ireland last month, where she was present as a reporter on Air Force One.
Anna Kelly, the White House principal deputy press secretary, confirmed Harmony's new role in a statement.

Swyer syndrome is a rare condition in which a person is born with XY chromosomes, the combination usually associated with males, but their reproductive organs develop along a typically female pattern. The person typically has female external anatomy and a uterus and fallopian tubes.
The condition often goes unnoticed during childhood and comes to light during adolescence, when puberty does not progress normally or menstruation does not begin. It can also be diagnosed later during investigations for infertility. Here’s all you need to know about Swyer syndrome.
What is Swyer syndrome?
Swyer syndrome is a rare difference of sex development, medically known as 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis. According to the US’ Genetic and Rare Diseases Information Center, a person with the condition has a 46,XY chromosome pattern, but the gonads do not develop into functioning testes. Instead, they remain as small, non-functioning structures called “streak gonads”. The person generally develops female external genitalia, while the uterus and fallopian tubes are usually present. The condition is estimated to occur in about one in 80,000 people,
Swyer syndrome results from disruption of the genetic pathway involved in testicular development during early embryonic development. The SRY gene, located on the Y chromosome, plays an important role in initiating this process. However, an SRY mutation is not found in every person with Swyer syndrome.
What are the symptoms?
Swyer syndrome may not be apparent during childhood and often comes to light during adolescence, when puberty does not progress normally. One of the most characteristic signs is primary amenorrhoea, meaning that menstruation does not begin.
Delayed or incomplete development of secondary sexual characteristics can also prompt investigation. Because the streak gonads do not produce sufficient sex hormones, spontaneous breast development may be limited. The condition can sometimes remain undiagnosed even when a person reaches adulthood.
How is Swyer syndrome diagnosed?
Diagnosis usually involves looking at the person’s chromosomes, hormone levels and reproductive anatomy. Karyotyping, a test that examines the number and structure of chromosomes, typically shows a 46,XY pattern in Swyer syndrome. Blood tests generally show evidence of gonadal failure, including low levels of sex hormones and elevated levels of hormones such as follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinising hormone. Ultrasound or MRI can be used to examine the uterus and the gonads.
Genetic testing can be used to investigate the underlying cause, including variants in SRY and other genes involved in gonadal development. However, not finding an SRY mutation does not exclude Swyer syndrome. In some patients, even more extensive genetic testing may not identify the precise molecular cause.
Can Swyer syndrome be treated?
There is currently no treatment that can change the 46,XY chromosome pattern or turn the streak gonads into functioning ovaries. However, the effects of Swyer syndrome can be effectively managed. Hormone replacement therapy, usually involving oestrogen and subsequently an appropriate progestogen regimen when indicated, is used to induce and maintain puberty, support development of secondary sexual characteristics and protect bone health.
The streak gonads also need to be assessed because they carry an increased risk of gonadoblastoma, a type of germ-cell tumour. Decisions about gonadectomy and its timing are now generally individualised according to the underlying diagnosis and tumour risk.
Fertility is another important consideration. Because the streak gonads cannot produce eggs, people with Swyer syndrome cannot conceive using their own eggs. However, if the uterus is present and sufficiently developed, pregnancy can be possible through IVF using a donated egg or embryo. Research shows that patients with Swyer syndrome can have successful pregnancies following endometrial preparation with hormones and IVF using donated eggs. Following pregnancy and delivery, continued hormone replacement is important for maintaining bone health.
In other words, Swyer syndrome itself cannot currently be reversed, but its effects can be managed. Hormone replacement can address the absence of normal gonadal hormones, removal of the streak gonads can reduce the risk of tumours, and assisted reproductive techniques can make pregnancy possible for some patients.

Wakefield beat Warrington to win Super League
- Published
Betfred Super League Grand Final
Warrington (0) 10
Tries: Lindop 2 Goal: Irwin
Wakefield (19) 23
Tries: Scott, Vagana, Tevaga, Johnstone Goals: Jowitt 3 Drop goal: Sinfield
Wakefield Trinity became only the sixth, and most unlikely, club to win the Super League title after a deserved win over Warrington Wolves.
Only two years after being in the Championship and in their first ever Grand Final, Wakefield took to the Old Trafford stage as if they were to the manor born.
Daryl Powell's side did the bulk of the damage in a devastating first half as they raced into a 19-0 lead on their way to becoming champions of England for the first time since 1968, long before the Super League era.
Trinity carried on from where they had left off in the semi-final against Wigan Warriors with tries from Cameron Scott, Isaiah Vagana and Jazz Tevaga and a drop goal from Jack Sinfield.
Arron Lindop's try gave Warrington brief hope early in the second half, but when Tom Johnstone went over at the other end, the game was up despite Lindop's second try late on.
Wakefield guarantee legendary status
This is a final few would have predicted seven days ago, let alone at any point throughout the season.
But Warrington snuck past Leeds Rhinos, and Wakefield Trinity then stunned the whole of rugby league as they demolished Wigan on the Warriors' own patch to make it to Old Trafford.
While Warrington have been close in previous years, Wakefield have been spectacular bolters in 2026.
Only two years ago, they were winning the Championship play-off final before their place in Super League was confirmed by the IMG grading system, having been relegated in 2023.
They were sixth last year and went two places better this season before memorable play-off successes over Leigh Leopards and then the Warriors.
In the build-up during the week, Powell had challenged his players to earn legendary status, knowing that was their long-term reward if they could emerge victorious.
After scoring 33 unanswered points in a spell at Wigan, Wakefield simply brought that momentum with them to Old Trafford as they absolutely bossed the first half, stretching that streak to 52 points.
Johnstone had already had one try denied by a TV review before Lachlan Walmsley's brilliant reverse pass sent Scott over to score.
And in a period where everything they did was working, Jake Trueman's high kick on the last tackle was spectacularly caught by Johnstone above opposite wing Albert Hopoate and tapped back for the supporting Vagana to dive over.
They were overpowering their opponents, exemplified by Tevaga being unstoppable from close to the posts for their third try.
And showing the sort of game smarts his revered father Sir Kevin Sinfield had in his Leeds Rhinos days, son Jack added an extra point to keep the scoreboard ticking as the half closed to leave Warrington needing more than three converted tries.
Warrington bridesmaids for a fifth time
In the Super League era, Warrington have been the eternal bridesmaids, watching on as traditional rivals Wigan and St Helens have swept up the silverware.
This was their fifth Grand Final, and felt like the chance to finally get their hands on the big prize and be champions for the first time since 1955.
Under head coach Sam Burgess, they had lost Challenge Cup finals at Wembley in the previous two years, but they had arrived at this game on the back of nine wins out of 10.
Crucially that sole defeat had been at Wakefield in round 26 of the regular season and in the opening 40 minutes, they had few answers.
But a high tackle by Trinity centre Corey Hall resulted in him being sin-binned early in the second period and, with a man extra, Lindop went over to offer a glimmer of a comeback.
However, Warrington could not score again with that momentum. Wakefield weathered the storm and, with numbers levelled up, they worked an opening for Johnstone's power and pace to deliver the decisive try.
Lindop went over again for his second as the Wolves desperately attacked, but with Ewan Irwin missing the conversion, Trinity players and staff were able to count down until the final whistle before celebrations could begin as Warrington's wait for another title now extends to a 72nd year.

Co-pilot in FlyDubai incident is identified as Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami
The co-pilot suspected of stabbing the captain on an Israel-bound FlyDubai flight has been identified as an Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami
CAIRO -- The co-pilot suspected of stabbing the captain of an Israel-bound FlyDubai flight before passengers and others stopped the attack is an Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami, three people with knowledge of the situation, including a Gulf and Western diplomat, said on Saturday.
All spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
The Gulf diplomat said investigations are underway to establish whether he acted as a “lone wolf or has any connection with any extremist groups.”
The co-pilot, who officials said nearly crashed the sharply plummeting flight with 182 people aboard, was barred from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views, a person familiar with the matter said.
The co-pilot was then hired by the United Arab Emirates-based airline FlyDubai, the person said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss the ongoing investigation. It was not immediately clear to what extent he was vetted when he was hired. Oman’s barring of him was first reported by The Wall Street Journal.
How the co-pilot managed to be working in the cockpit on Wednesday morning is a central question for investigators.
Israel says has it has long-standing agreements with foreign carriers to keep pilots from flying into the country if they are citizens of nations that don’t maintain diplomatic relations with Israel. Israel and Oman do not have formal diplomatic relations.
There was no immediate comment from FlyDubai, the UAE government or Oman Air. Oman’s government has said nothing publicly in response to repeated questions since the incident.
UAE senior diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash on Friday called the attack a “dangerous terrorist act” in a post on X. The incident is a test for the UAE government, which has earned a reputation for effective measures against extremist activities but has also bristled in the past over criticism of security lapses.
Little else was immediately known about the co-pilot’s background. His Instagram account was active until the day of the flight and then deleted.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday said the co-pilot had undergone “Islamist radicalization,” but provided no evidence.
The captain, who was badly wounded, has said he used his remaining energy while being stabbed to unlock the cockpit door, allowing people who had noticed alarmingly unusual sounds to come in, tackle the co-pilot and stabilize the plane. It made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
Investigators have not publicly identified the object used to stab the captain or said whether it was carried onto the plane or came from inside the aircraft.
Both the captain and co-pilot were later taken to the UAE as it leads the investigation. Officials have said a number of countries including Israel are participating.
___
Mednick reported from Tel Aviv, Israel. AP Washington bureau chief Anna Johnson contributed to this report from Washington.
